facts.pair.description: Joins two short independent facts on one line of a project's page, for example "3 involved · 2 underway" or "Voted yes · swipe up for the next". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the separator between them is translated.

sentences.pair.description: Joins two complete sentences into one short paragraph on a project's page, for example a note under the list of categories. {{first}} is every sentence so far and {{second}} the next one, each already ending in its own full stop. Only the space between sentences is translated; leave it out if your language writes none.

page.title.needsYou.description: Title of a project's Needs you page: the feed of decisions waiting on this person, one per screen (changes to vote on, requests nobody has taken).

page.title.allItems.description: Title shown in the back bar of a project's All items page: the whole board of requests and proposals, opened from the Workshop tab.

page.title.plan.description: Title of the page that shows the plan for a project's first version, opened from its Hub.

page.title.bot.description: Title of the page under a project's Workshop that lists what holds each of Homeroom bot's slots on the project and what waits for one.

botSlots.door.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Link at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card that opens the page, and the first of its facts, which are shown joined by a middle dot: how many builds the bot has waiting or under way on the project. {{used}} is how many, {{cap}} how many it may have at once.

botSlots.doorVotes_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. One of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after "Homeroom bot: building 3 of 5" and a middle dot: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.doorVotes_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. One of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after "Homeroom bot: building 3 of 5" and a middle dot: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.doorWaiting_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. The last of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after a middle dot, when requests the bot is ready to build wait for a slot. {{count}} is how many requests wait.

botSlots.doorWaiting_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. The last of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after a middle dot, when requests the bot is ready to build wait for a slot. {{count}} is how many requests wait.

botSlots.slots.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the card listing what holds each slot.

botSlots.slots.building.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card: how many builds the bot has waiting or under way on the project, of how many it may have at once. {{used}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.votes_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card, under the builds: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote or being merged, of how many it may have waiting at once. {{count}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.votes_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card, under the builds: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote or being merged, of how many it may have waiting at once. {{count}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.frees.text: A build frees its slot when it is done. A change waiting for votes frees one when it merges or is withdrawn, or when its request closes.
botSlots.slots.frees.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note in the Slots card saying what frees each kind of slot: a build's, and a change's that waits for votes.

botSlots.slots.empty.text: No slots in use: a request found ready is built at once.
botSlots.slots.empty.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note in the Slots card when nothing holds a slot.

botSlots.waiting.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests that are ready but wait for a slot, in the order the bot will take them up.

botSlots.taken.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot had found ready but that a person has taken since: the bot leaves them alone, so they do not wait for a slot.

botSlots.waitingOn.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests where the bot waits on a person: a question for them to answer, or a plan waiting for them to tap Build it.

botSlots.upNext.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot will read next, in order: those waiting in its queue, then the project's older requests.

botSlots.upNext.note.text: Older requests are read one at a time, while a slot is free and nothing newer waits.
botSlots.upNext.note.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note under the Up next heading when it lists older requests: requests filed before the bot started building for everyone, which it now reads one by one when it has room.

botSlots.stopped.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot tried to build that stopped: the build failed, or ended with no change to show.

botSlots.leftToPeople.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot read and judged need a person rather than the bot: a decision to make, or nothing it can build.

botSlots.onHold.title.text: On hold until the week resets
botSlots.onHold.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests on hold because whoever pays for them has used up this week's building time.

botSlots.limits.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the card with the limits that hold work back.

botSlots.limits.week.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Label in the Limits card for the signed-in person's own building time this week.

botSlots.limits.weekUsed.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How much of the signed-in person's building time this week is used. {{percent}} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

botSlots.limits.weekResets.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. When the signed-in person's building time resets. {{date}} is a short weekday, date and time.

botSlots.limits.weekUnlimited.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Shown in place of how much is used when the signed-in person's building time has no weekly limit.

botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_one.text: Up to {{count}} build at once on this project
botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many builds the bot runs on the project at the same time. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_other.text: Up to {{count}} builds at once on this project
botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many builds the bot runs on the project at the same time. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.reading_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many requests wait for the bot to read them. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.reading_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many requests wait for the bot to read them. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.off.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot is switched off everywhere.

botSlots.notHere.text: Homeroom bot doesn't build changes on this project.
botSlots.notHere.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot does not act on this project.

botSlots.paused.text: Homeroom bot is paused on this project.
botSlots.paused.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot is paused on this project.

botSlots.loadFailed.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Shown when the page could not be read.

botSlots.untitled.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. A request's row when it has no title. {{number}} is its number.

botSlots.meta.asked.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under a request's title naming who asked for it. {{username}} is their username.

botSlots.meta.waiting.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of a request waiting for a slot: how long it has waited. {{span}} is a short span of time such as "3h 20m" or "2d 4h".

botSlots.meta.taken.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of a request a person has taken: how long ago they took it (claimed it, or started a change of their own for it). {{span}} is a short span of time such as "3h 20m" or "2d 4h".

botSlots.older.next.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: it is the next of the older requests the bot will read.

botSlots.older.ahead_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: how many older requests the bot will read before this one. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.older.ahead_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: how many older requests the bot will read before this one. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.older.trialReady.text: found ready in its trial run
botSlots.older.trialReady.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next, after its place: before the bot started building for everyone, it read this request in a trial and found it ready to build.

botSlots.older.trialQuestion.text: had a question in its trial run
botSlots.older.trialQuestion.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next, after its place: before the bot started building for everyone, it read this request in a trial and had a question about it.

botSlots.older.notRead.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next, after its place: the bot has not read this request at all yet.

botSlots.older.badge.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Words for screen readers on the small square beside an older request in Up next: it waits its turn to be read.

botSlots.showAll.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Button at the end of a long section of requests that shows the rest of them. {{count}} is how many requests the section has in all.

botSlots.withPeople_one.text: {{count}} more open request is with a person who took it on.
botSlots.withPeople_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Line after the sections of requests: how many other open requests a person has taken on (claimed, or a change of their own), which the bot leaves to them. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.withPeople_other.text: {{count}} more open requests are with people who took them on.
botSlots.withPeople_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Line after the sections of requests: how many other open requests people have taken on (claimed, or a change of their own), which the bot leaves to them. {{count}} is that number.

page.title.workshop.description: Title of a project's Workshop page: the build tab beside its Hub, where the open work, the approval rule and recent changes are listed. A noun, the name of the tab.

page.loading.description: Accessible label of the placeholder cards drawn while a project's page is still loading. Workshop here is the project's build page, a noun.

page.backToWorkshop.description: Label of the back button at the top of a project's All items page: it names where the button goes, the project's Workshop tab. A noun.

allItems.lane.more_one.description: Note at the end of a lane inside an unfolded category on a project's All items page, when the lane holds more items than are drawn. A lane is one stage of work within the category (open, underway, in review, shipped). {{count}} is how many are not shown; keep the plus sign.

allItems.lane.more_other.description: Note at the end of a lane inside an unfolded category on a project's All items page, when the lane holds more items than are drawn. A lane is one stage of work within the category (open, underway, in review, shipped). {{count}} is how many are not shown; keep the plus sign.

allItems.theme.whoInvolved.description: Accessible name of the row of initials on a category card on a project's All items page; pressing it lists the people. {{people}} is their usernames, already joined into a list.

allItems.theme.chip.fresh_one.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many items in the category are new since this person's last visit. <0></0> makes the number bold; keep the plus sign.

allItems.theme.chip.fresh_other.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many items in the category are new since this person's last visit. <0></0> makes the number bold; keep the plus sign.

allItems.theme.chip.review_one.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are proposals being reviewed or voted on. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.review_other.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are proposals being reviewed or voted on. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.underway_one.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items somebody is working on now. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.underway_other.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items somebody is working on now. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.open_one.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are open and not yet picked up. Open is an adjective here (not yet done). <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.open_other.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are open and not yet picked up. Open is an adjective here (not yet done). <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.shipped_one.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its changes were merged and went live in the app this week. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.chip.shipped_other.description: Count chip on a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its changes were merged and went live in the app this week. <0></0> makes the number bold.

allItems.theme.stat.people_one.description: Figure on a category card on a project's All items page: how many people are involved in the category. <0></0> is the large number and the word is its small label; the layout puts the gap between them, so no space is written.

allItems.theme.stat.people_other.description: Figure on a category card on a project's All items page: how many people are involved in the category. <0></0> is the large number and the word is its small label; the layout puts the gap between them, so no space is written.

allItems.theme.stat.items_one.description: Figure on a category card on a project's All items page: how many items (requests and proposals) in the category are still open. <0></0> is the large number and the word is its small label; the layout puts the gap between them, so no space is written.

allItems.theme.stat.items_other.description: Figure on a category card on a project's All items page: how many items (requests and proposals) in the category are still open. <0></0> is the large number and the word is its small label; the layout puts the gap between them, so no space is written.

allItems.theme.foot.involved_one.description: First fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many people are involved in the category. Another fact follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.involved_other.description: First fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many people are involved in the category. Another fact follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.underway_one.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items somebody is working on now. It follows other facts after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.underway_other.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items somebody is working on now. It follows other facts after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.review_one.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are proposals being reviewed or voted on. It follows other facts after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.review_other.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page: how many of its items are proposals being reviewed or voted on. It follows other facts after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.shippedIdle_one.text: {{count}} went live this week, nothing in progress now
allItems.theme.foot.shippedIdle_one.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page, when nobody is working in the category right now but changes were merged this week. {{count}} is how many changes went live. It follows another fact after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.shippedIdle_other.text: {{count}} went live this week, nothing in progress now
allItems.theme.foot.shippedIdle_other.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page, when nobody is working in the category right now but changes were merged this week. {{count}} is how many changes went live. It follows another fact after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.quiet_one.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page, when nothing has happened in the category for more than two weeks. {{count}} is the number of days (always over 14). It follows another fact after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.quiet_other.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page, when nothing has happened in the category for more than two weeks. {{count}} is the number of days (always over 14). It follows another fact after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.foot.idle.description: Fact on the bottom line of a category card on a project's All items page, when nobody is working on anything in the category at the moment. It follows another fact after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.theme.openOnBoard.description: Link at the bottom of an unfolded category on a project's All items page: shows this category's items on the board laid out by stage. Open is a verb; keep the trailing arrow.

allItems.theme.hiddenThenOpen_one.description: Bottom line of an unfolded category on a project's All items page when some of its items are not drawn. <0></0> is the note saying how many, ending in its separator; <1></1> is the link that shows the category's items on the board laid out by stage (Open is a verb). Keep the plus sign and the trailing arrow.

allItems.theme.hiddenThenOpen_other.description: Bottom line of an unfolded category on a project's All items page when some of its items are not drawn. <0></0> is the note saying how many, ending in its separator; <1></1> is the link that shows the category's items on the board laid out by stage (Open is a verb). Keep the plus sign and the trailing arrow.

allItems.categories.draftedAt.text: Categories were drafted {{when}} and are re-drafted daily, or sooner when a tenth of the board changes.
allItems.categories.draftedAt.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, when an AI model grouped the items. {{when}} is how long ago, already written out, for example "3d ago" or "Jun 16".

allItems.categories.drafted.text: Categories are drafted from the board and re-drafted daily, or sooner when a tenth of the board changes.
allItems.categories.drafted.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, when an AI model grouped the items and the time of the last draft is not known.

allItems.categories.pending_one.description: Sentence in the footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many new items the AI model is still sorting into a category. A card is one item (a request or a proposal) on the board.

allItems.categories.pending_other.description: Sentence in the footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many new items the AI model is still sorting into a category. A card is one item (a request or a proposal) on the board.

allItems.categories.unplaced_one.text: {{count}} card did not fit a category and waits for the next draft.
allItems.categories.unplaced_one.description: Sentence in the footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many items the AI model could not put in any category. They stay ungrouped until the categories are drafted again.

allItems.categories.unplaced_other.text: {{count}} cards did not fit a category and wait for the next draft.
allItems.categories.unplaced_other.description: Sentence in the footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many items the AI model could not put in any category. They stay ungrouped until the categories are drafted again.

allItems.categories.lastError.text: The last attempt failed ({{error}}); it is retried shortly.
allItems.categories.lastError.description: Sentence in the footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, when the AI model's last try at grouping the items failed. {{error}} is the technical reason as the server reported it, not translated.

allItems.categories.demo.text: Staging demo grouping: in production the categories are drafted by the model from the board.
allItems.categories.demo.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, shown only on a test (staging) copy of Homeroom where the categories are sample data.

allItems.categories.beingDrafted.text: Categories are being drafted from the board now. They replace this grouping when they land.
allItems.categories.beingDrafted.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, while an AI model is writing categories for the first time and the items are grouped by a simpler fallback.

allItems.categories.draftFailed.text: The last attempt to draft categories failed ({{error}}). Items stay grouped by the categories the group has voted for until the next attempt.
allItems.categories.draftFailed.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, when the AI model could not write categories. {{error}} is the technical reason as the server reported it, not translated.

allItems.categories.noModel.text: No AI model is configured, so items are grouped by the categories the group has voted for.
allItems.categories.noModel.description: Footnote under the list of categories on a project's All items page, when no AI model is set up to group the items.

allItems.grouping.categories_one.description: First fact on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many categories the items are grouped into. Other facts may follow it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.categories_other.description: First fact on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page: how many categories the items are grouped into. Other facts may follow it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.byCategoryForNow.description: Fact on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page, when the items are grouped by the category the group voted for each one because the AI model has not grouped them yet. It follows the count of categories after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.demo.description: Fact on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page, shown only on a test (staging) copy of Homeroom where the categories are sample data. It follows the count of categories after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.placing.description: Progress note on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page, while the AI model sorts new items into categories. It follows other facts after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.redrafting.description: Progress note on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page, while the AI model writes the categories again. It follows other facts after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.grouping.drafting.description: Progress note on the small line above the list of categories on a project's All items page, while the AI model writes the categories for the first time. It follows other facts after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

allItems.sort.label.description: Accessible name of the group of three buttons above the list of categories on a project's All items page that choose the order the categories are listed in. Order is a verb.

allItems.sort.people.description: Button above the list of categories on a project's All items page: lists the categories with the most people involved first.

allItems.sort.activity.description: Button above the list of categories on a project's All items page: lists the most recently active categories first.

allItems.sort.open.description: Button above the list of categories on a project's All items page: lists the categories with the most open (not yet done) items first.

allItems.group.label.description: Accessible name of the two tabs at the top of a project's All items page that choose how the items are grouped: by category or by stage. Group is a verb.

allItems.group.category.description: Name of an icon tab at the top of a project's All items page: groups the items by what part of the project they are about. Read as the tab's tooltip and by screen readers.

allItems.group.stage.description: Name of an icon tab at the top of a project's All items page: groups the items into columns by how far along they are (open, in progress, voting, done). Read as the tab's tooltip and by screen readers.

boardEmpty.filtered.text: Nothing here matches the current search and filters.
boardEmpty.filtered.description: Note shown in place of the items on a project's Hub or All items page when the search box or the filters hide every item.

boardEmpty.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load open requests right now. <0></0>
boardEmpty.loadFailed.description: Note shown in place of the items on a project's Hub or All items page when the list of open requests could not be fetched. There is no button in it. <0></0> is not a control: it is the place where a second, separate and complete sentence is drawn right after this one, namely one of the "Nothing on the board yet…" messages (which has its own entry and its own link styling). Keep the tag empty and put it after this sentence, with whatever your language writes between two sentences.

boardEmpty.readOnly.description: Note shown in place of the items on a project's Hub or All items page when the project has no requests or proposals, for a person who can only look. The board is the project's list of work.

boardEmpty.start.description: Button under the note on a project's Hub or All items page when the project has no requests or proposals, for a person who builds changes here. It opens a new session to build a change. "Change" is a noun.

boardEmpty.startBot.text: Tell Homeroom bot what to change
boardEmpty.startBot.description: Button under the note on a project's Hub or All items page when the project has no requests or proposals, for a person Homeroom bot builds changes for on this project. It opens their chat with Homeroom bot with this project attached. Keep "Homeroom bot" as it is; here "change" is a verb.

boardEmpty.press.hub.collab.full.text: Nothing on the board yet. Press <0>⋯</0> to suggest an improvement or import a PR; to make one yourself, use Build it now there.
boardEmpty.press.hub.collab.full.description: Note on a project's Hub when the project has no requests or proposals. <0>⋯</0> is the Hub's own More button, shown as its three-dot sign. "Suggest an improvement", "Import a PR" (a GitHub pull request) and "Build it now" are rows of that menu.

boardEmpty.press.hub.plain.full.text: Nothing on the board yet. Press <0>⋯</0> to suggest an improvement; to make one yourself, use Build it now there.
boardEmpty.press.hub.plain.full.description: Note on a project's Hub when the project has no requests or proposals. <0>⋯</0> is the Hub's own More button, shown as its three-dot sign. "Suggest an improvement" and "Build it now" are rows of that menu.

boardEmpty.press.away.collab.full.text: Nothing on the board yet. Press <0>⋯</0> on the hub to suggest an improvement or import a PR; to make one yourself, use Build it now there.
boardEmpty.press.away.collab.full.description: Note on a project's All items page when the project has no requests or proposals. <0>⋯</0> is the More button on the project's Hub, shown as its three-dot sign. "Suggest an improvement", "Import a PR" (a GitHub pull request) and "Build it now" are rows of that menu.

boardEmpty.press.away.plain.full.text: Nothing on the board yet. Press <0>⋯</0> on the hub to suggest an improvement; to make one yourself, use Build it now there.
boardEmpty.press.away.plain.full.description: Note on a project's All items page when the project has no requests or proposals. <0>⋯</0> is the More button on the project's Hub, shown as its three-dot sign. "Suggest an improvement" and "Build it now" are rows of that menu.

hub.startHere.title.description: Heading of the prompt at the top of a project's Hub when nothing is open and nothing has ever been merged, for a person Homeroom bot does not build changes for on this project.

hub.startHere.text.text: Nothing is open and nothing has shipped yet. The first change is yours to start.
hub.startHere.text.description: Text of the prompt at the top of a project's Hub when the project has no open items and no merged change, for a person Homeroom bot does not build changes for on this project. Shipped means merged and live in the app.

hub.startHere.start.description: Button in the prompt at the top of an unstarted project's Hub: opens a new session with a coding agent to build a change to the app. Change is a noun.

hub.startHere.bot.title.text: What do you want to change?
hub.startHere.bot.title.description: Heading of the card at the top of a project's Hub when nothing is open and nothing has ever been merged, for a person Homeroom bot builds changes for there. "Change" is a verb; the project is what changes.

hub.startHere.bot.text.text: Say it in your own words. Homeroom bot makes the change for you.
hub.startHere.bot.text.description: Text of the card at the top of a project's Hub when nothing is open and nothing has ever been merged, under the heading "What do you want to change?". "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant, which builds changes to the project; keep it as it is. "Change" is a noun here.

hub.startHere.bot.button.text: Tell Homeroom bot what to change
hub.startHere.bot.button.description: Button on the card at the top of a project's Hub when nothing is open and nothing has ever been merged: opens the person's chat with Homeroom bot (the assistant's name; keep it as it is) with this project attached, ready for them to type what they want changed. "Change" is a verb.

hub.card.close.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the small close (✕) button at the top right of two cards on a project's hub: "Share it" and "What do you want to change?". Closing one hides it on that project for good; what it offered stays elsewhere on the page.

hub.update.title.description: Title of the card on a version's hub (a project made from another, the original) when the original has changed and that change is ready to look at. {{project}} is the original's name.

hub.update.titleBehind.text: {{project}} has changed since you made this
hub.update.titleBehind.description: Title of the card on the hub of a version that does not get the original's updates, shown once when the original has changed since. {{project}} is the original's name.

hub.update.behindLine.text: Your version doesn’t get its updates on its own. See what changed, then vote on it if you want it.
hub.update.behindLine.description: Line on the card of a version that does not get the original's updates, under "has changed since you made this".

hub.update.ready.text: Its changes are ready for you to try and vote on.
hub.update.ready.description: Line on the Update card when it lists none of the original's changes by name.

hub.update.bringsMore_one.description: Line on the Update card: the first of the original's changes it brings, {{title}}, and how many more there are, {{count}}.

hub.update.bringsMore_other.description: Line on the Update card: the first of the original's changes it brings, {{title}}, and how many more there are, {{count}}.

hub.update.clash_one.text: It clashes with your own changes in {{count}} file, so it needs fitting to your version first.
hub.update.clash_one.description: Line on the Update card when the original's change and the version's own changes touch the same file. {{count}} is how many files.

hub.update.clash_other.text: It clashes with your own changes in {{count}} files, so it needs fitting to your version first.
hub.update.clash_other.description: Line on the Update card when the original's change and the version's own changes touch the same files. {{count}} is how many files.

hub.update.see.description: Button on the Update card: puts the original's change up as a change on this version and opens it.

hub.update.opening.description: Label of the Update card's "See the update" button while the change is being made.

hub.update.notNow.description: Button on the Update card: hides the card on this device.

hub.update.fit.text: Ask Homeroom bot to fit it
hub.update.fit.description: Button on the Update card and on the update's own page when the original's change clashes with the version's own: asks Homeroom bot to build it to fit this version, as a request. Homeroom bot is the product's assistant; keep the name.

hub.update.fitAsked.text: Homeroom bot is on it. <0>See the request</0>
hub.update.fitAsked.description: Shown on the Update card once Homeroom bot was asked to fit the update. The tagged words link to the request it builds. "See" is a verb.

hub.update.failed.description: Error on the Update card when its button's request failed and the server gave no reason.

hub.versions.title.description: Small-caps heading of the section on a project's hub about the versions others have made of it: what they suggest, what they have been making, and how its last update went.

hub.versions.suggestions.title.description: Row in the "From its versions" section: changes the versions have sent to this project for it to take.

hub.versions.suggestions.from.description: Second line of the Suggestions row: the one suggestion, {{title}}, and the version that sent it, {{version}}.

hub.versions.suggestions.fromPrivate.description: Second line of the Suggestions row: the one suggestion, {{title}}, sent by a version whose name is not shown.

hub.versions.suggestions.more_one.description: Second line of the Suggestions row: the first suggestion, {{title}}, and how many more there are, {{count}}.

hub.versions.suggestions.more_other.description: Second line of the Suggestions row: the first suggestion, {{title}}, and how many more there are, {{count}}.

hub.versions.lately.title.description: Row in the "From its versions" section: changes that went live lately in the versions made of this project.

hub.versions.lately.first.description: Second line of the "Lately in its versions" row: the newest change, {{title}}, and the version it went live in, {{version}}.

hub.versions.lately.firstMore_one.description: Second line of the "Lately in its versions" row: the newest change, {{title}}, the version it went live in, {{version}}, and how many more changes there were, {{count}}.

hub.versions.lately.firstMore_other.description: Second line of the "Lately in its versions" row: the newest change, {{title}}, the version it went live in, {{version}}, and how many more changes there were, {{count}}.

hub.versions.last.title.description: Row in the "From its versions" section: how this project's last change went down in the versions that get its updates.

hub.versions.last.all.description: Second line of the "Your last update" row. {{offered}} is how many versions were given the update, {{took}} how many took it, {{skipped}} how many skipped it and {{deciding}} how many have not decided yet.

hub.versions.last.noSkipped.description: Second line of the "Your last update" row when none skipped it. {{offered}} is how many versions were given the update, {{took}} how many took it and {{deciding}} how many have not decided yet.

hub.versions.last.noDeciding.description: Second line of the "Your last update" row when every version has decided. {{offered}} is how many versions were given the update, {{took}} how many took it and {{skipped}} how many skipped it.

hub.versions.last.took.description: Second line of the "Your last update" row when none skipped it and every version has decided. {{offered}} is how many versions were given the update and {{took}} how many took it.

workshop.allItems.title.description: Heading of the first section on a project's Workshop tab: the four figures about the project's requests and proposals.

workshop.part.overview.description: Small-caps label over the first part of the Workshop tab of a project's page: the All items card with its figures, where the open work is, and the approval rule.

workshop.part.happened.description: Small-caps label over the last part of the Workshop tab of a project's page: this week's changes and requests row by row, then one row for each week before it.

workshop.allItems.seeAll.description: Button at the end of the All items heading on a project's Workshop tab: opens the All items page, the whole board of requests and proposals.

workshop.allItems.seeAllFiltered.description: The See all button on a project's Workshop tab while a search or filter is still set on the All items page it opens. <0></0> is a small dot (keep it empty); <1></1> is read only by screen readers and adds that the list is filtered.

workshop.dash.open_one.description: Label under the first large figure on a project's Workshop tab: the number of open requests and proposals. The number is drawn above it, so it is not in the text.

workshop.dash.open_other.description: Label under the first large figure on a project's Workshop tab: the number of open requests and proposals. The number is drawn above it, so it is not in the text.

workshop.dash.unclaimed.description: Label under the second large figure on a project's Workshop tab: how many of the open items nobody has taken on. The number is drawn above it; "them" is the open items counted by the figure before.

workshop.dash.votes_one.description: Label under the third large figure on a project's Workshop tab: how many proposals are waiting for votes. The number is drawn above it, so it is not in the text.

workshop.dash.votes_other.description: Label under the third large figure on a project's Workshop tab: how many proposals are waiting for votes. The number is drawn above it, so it is not in the text.

workshop.dash.shipped.description: Label under the fourth large figure on a project's Workshop tab: how many changes were merged and went live in the app this week. The number is drawn above it.

workshop.dash.shippedPartial.text: At least this many: there is more history than the page loaded.
workshop.dash.shippedPartial.description: Tooltip on the "live this week" figure on a project's Workshop tab, when the number is a lower bound (it is drawn with a plus sign after it).

workshop.dash.shippedWeek.text: This calendar week, counted from Monday 00:00 UTC.
workshop.dash.shippedWeek.description: Tooltip on the "live this week" figure on a project's Workshop tab: says which week is counted. UTC is the time zone.

workshop.dash.onYou_one.description: Line under the "waiting on votes" figure on the Workshop tab of a project's page: how many of those proposals wait on the viewer's own vote. {{count}} is that number, never zero.

workshop.dash.onYou_other.description: Line under the "waiting on votes" figure on the Workshop tab of a project's page: how many of those proposals wait on the viewer's own vote. {{count}} is that number, never zero.

workshop.dash.fromLastWeek_one.description: Line under the "live this week" figure on the Workshop tab of a project's page, beside an up or down arrow: how many changes went live last week, for comparison. {{count}} is last week's number.

workshop.dash.fromLastWeek_other.description: Line under the "live this week" figure on the Workshop tab of a project's page, beside an up or down arrow: how many changes went live last week, for comparison. {{count}} is last week's number.

workshop.pace.nonePartial.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: no change has been merged this week. Landed means merged into the app.

workshop.pace.atLeast_one.text: At least {{count}} change landed this week.
workshop.pace.atLeast_one.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: a lower bound on how many changes were merged this week, used when the full history was not loaded. Change is a noun; landed means merged into the app.

workshop.pace.atLeast_other.text: At least {{count}} changes landed this week.
workshop.pace.atLeast_other.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: a lower bound on how many changes were merged this week, used when the full history was not loaded. Change is a noun; landed means merged into the app.

workshop.pace.noneFortnight.text: Nothing has landed in the last fortnight.
workshop.pace.noneFortnight.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: no change was merged this week or the week before. A fortnight is two weeks.

workshop.pace.firstInFortnight_one.text: {{count}} change landed this week, the first in a fortnight.
workshop.pace.firstInFortnight_one.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: how many changes were merged this week, when none were merged the week before. Change is a noun; a fortnight is two weeks.

workshop.pace.firstInFortnight_other.text: {{count}} changes landed this week, the first in a fortnight.
workshop.pace.firstInFortnight_other.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: how many changes were merged this week, when none were merged the week before. Change is a noun; a fortnight is two weeks.

workshop.pace.up_one.text: {{count}} landed this week, up from {{previous}} the week before.
workshop.pace.up_one.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: more changes were merged this week ({{count}}) than the week before ({{previous}}).

workshop.pace.up_other.text: {{count}} landed this week, up from {{previous}} the week before.
workshop.pace.up_other.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: more changes were merged this week ({{count}}) than the week before ({{previous}}).

workshop.pace.down_one.text: {{count}} landed this week, down from {{previous}} the week before.
workshop.pace.down_one.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: fewer changes were merged this week ({{count}}) than the week before ({{previous}}).

workshop.pace.down_other.text: {{count}} landed this week, down from {{previous}} the week before.
workshop.pace.down_other.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: fewer changes were merged this week ({{count}}) than the week before ({{previous}}).

workshop.pace.same_one.text: {{count}} landed this week, the same as the week before.
workshop.pace.same_one.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: as many changes were merged this week ({{count}}) as the week before.

workshop.pace.same_other.text: {{count}} landed this week, the same as the week before.
workshop.pace.same_other.description: Sentence of the fallback summary on a project's Workshop tab: as many changes were merged this week ({{count}}) as the week before.

workshop.desk.title.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The row's title.

workshop.desk.open.text: Opens Homeroom bot, showing your work in {{project}}
workshop.desk.open.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The row's tooltip. {{project}} is the project's name.

workshop.desk.both.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The count at the row's right end, in the Homeroom bot tab's own words: how many things wait on the person, and how many are being worked on. <0></0> marks the number that asks for them, drawn in the accent.

workshop.desk.needs.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The count at the row's right end when things wait on the person and nothing else is being worked on. <0></0> marks the number, drawn in the accent.

workshop.desk.progress.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The count at the row's right end when nothing waits on the person but some of their work is being worked on.

workshop.desk.waiting.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The count at the row's right end when the person's work only waits on somebody else (votes, a free builder).

workshop.desk.next.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The row's second line: the first thing that waits on the person. {{title}} is its title, written by a person.

workshop.desk.empty.text: Nothing of yours here right now.
workshop.desk.empty.description: The Your work row on a project's Workshop tab (a card of its own under Overview): how much of the person's own work there is in this project, opening the Homeroom bot tab (the platform's own assistant, whose page lists everything of theirs) narrowed to this project. The row's second line when none of the person's work is under way or waiting in this project.

hub.workshop.sub.description: The Workshop row of a project's Hub (For you): opens the project's Workshop, which shows what happened week by week and All items, the whole board. Not the person's own work, which has its own card on the Workshop tab (Your work).

workshop.fresh.buildIt.description: Button on a new request's row in the "New for you" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: starts building it, by asking Homeroom bot or with the viewer's own coding agent, whichever the request's own page offers.

workshop.fresh.workOnIt.description: Button on a new request's row in the "New for you" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: opens a thread only the viewer can see, in their chat with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant), about this request, as the request's own "Work on this with Homeroom bot" does. "Work on" is a verb.

workshop.private.title.description: Small-caps label over the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.note.text: Only platform admins can see these. They are kept in Homeroom, never on GitHub.
workshop.private.note.description: Grey line under the label of the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.badge.description: Short badge, beside a lock, on each row of the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.someone.description: Stands in for the author's name when the account is gone, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.comments_one.description: How many comments a private request has, on its row in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.comments_other.description: How many comments a private request has, on its row in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.noComments.description: Shown under an opened private request with no comments, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.commentPlaceholder.text: Add a comment for the admins
workshop.private.commentPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the comment box under an opened private request, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.comment.description: Button that posts the comment typed under an opened private request, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub. "Comment" is a verb.

workshop.private.close.description: Button that closes an opened private request (it is done or no longer needed), in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.loadFailed.description: Error under an opened private request when its comments could not be loaded, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

workshop.private.actionFailed.description: Error under an opened private request when posting a comment or closing it failed, in the "Private requests" section of a project's Workshop page, shown only to platform admins. A private request is one only platform admins can see, kept in Homeroom and never posted on GitHub.

since.none.text: Nothing new since you were last here.
since.none.description: Line in the Since your last visit section of a project's Workshop tab when nobody else has done anything since this person's last visit.

since.markAllSeen.description: Button beside the "What happened" label on the Workshop tab of a project's page: marks everything new since the viewer's last visit as seen. Disabled when nothing is new.

happened.allOfWeek.description: Button under this week's rows in the "What happened" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: opens this week's own page, with everything in it grouped.

happened.earlierWeeks.description: Button at the foot of the "What happened" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: lists more of the weeks before, one row each.

happened.row.new.description: Spoken name of the dot before a row in the "What happened" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: the item moved since the viewer's last visit.

happened.row.you.description: Small label on a row in the "What happened" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: the viewer made this change or request.

happened.row.goingLive.description: Small label on a row in the "What happened" card on the Workshop tab of a project's page: the change was merged and is still rolling out to the app.

since.week.thisWeek.description: Name of the current week, as the bold name of its row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab and as the title of that week's page. Its dates follow it.

since.week.rangeLive.description: The dates of the week still in progress, beside "This week" in the Week by week list of a project's Workshop tab and at the top of that week's page. {{start}} is the week's Monday, for example "Sep 14". Keep the arrow.

since.week.range.description: The dates of a finished week, as a row's name or beside it in the Week by week list of a project's Workshop tab and at the top of that week's page. {{start}} is its Monday and {{end}} its Sunday, for example "Aug 25 – Aug 31".

since.projectStarted.text: This project started the week of {{date}}.
since.projectStarted.description: Note under the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab, once every week is shown. {{date}} is the Monday of the project's first week, a short date such as "Aug 25" or "Aug 25, 2025".

weeks.lastWeek.description: Name of the previous calendar week, as the bold name of its row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab and as the title of that week's page.

weeks.row.fresh_one.description: Small mark on a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is how many things other people did in that week since this person's last visit.

weeks.row.fresh_other.description: Small mark on a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is how many things other people did in that week since this person's last visit.

weeks.row.live_one.description: Figure at the end of a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold.

weeks.row.live_other.description: Figure at the end of a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold.

weeks.row.liveAtLeast_one.description: Figure at the end of a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the plus sign after it: it means "at least".

weeks.row.liveAtLeast_other.description: Figure at the end of a week's row in the Week by week list on a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the plus sign after it: it means "at least".

weekPage.back.description: Label of the back button at the top of a week's page inside a project's Workshop tab: it names where the button goes, the Workshop tab itself. A noun, the name of the tab.

weekPage.meta.nowLive_one.description: Line under the title of this week's page in a project's Workshop tab: the week's dates so far, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is the week's Monday, for example "Sep 14". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the arrow.

weekPage.meta.nowLive_other.description: Line under the title of this week's page in a project's Workshop tab: the week's dates so far, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is the week's Monday, for example "Sep 14". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the arrow.

weekPage.meta.nowLiveAtLeast_one.description: Line under the title of this week's page in a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete: the week's dates so far, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is the week's Monday, for example "Sep 14". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the arrow, and the plus sign after the number: it means "at least".

weekPage.meta.nowLiveAtLeast_other.description: Line under the title of this week's page in a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete: the week's dates so far, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is the week's Monday, for example "Sep 14". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the arrow, and the plus sign after the number: it means "at least".

weekPage.meta.rangeLive_one.description: Line under the title of a finished week's page in a project's Workshop tab: the week's dates, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is its Monday and {{end}} its Sunday, for example "Aug 25 – Aug 31". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold.

weekPage.meta.rangeLive_other.description: Line under the title of a finished week's page in a project's Workshop tab: the week's dates, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is its Monday and {{end}} its Sunday, for example "Aug 25 – Aug 31". {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold.

weekPage.meta.rangeLiveAtLeast_one.description: Line under the title of a finished week's page in a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete: the week's dates, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is its Monday and {{end}} its Sunday. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the plus sign after the number: it means "at least".

weekPage.meta.rangeLiveAtLeast_other.description: Line under the title of a finished week's page in a project's Workshop tab, when the count is known to be incomplete: the week's dates, then how many changes went live. {{start}} is its Monday and {{end}} its Sunday. {{count}} is how many changes went live (were approved and became part of the running project) in that week; the tag makes the number bold. Keep the plus sign after the number: it means "at least".

weekPage.none.description: Line on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab when that week genuinely holds no requests, changes or other activity. Shown only after the week's list has finished loading and came back empty.

weekPage.loading.description: Line on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab while the page fetches what happened in that week. Shown under the week's summary line, in place of the list, until the rows arrive.

weekPage.failed.text: Some of this week could not be loaded. Open it again to try once more.
weekPage.failed.description: Line on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab when part of the week's history failed to load. Opening the week again retries; there is no separate retry button.

weekPage.group.new.description: Heading of the first group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: what other people did in that week after this person was last here.

weekPage.group.votes.description: Heading of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: proposed changes from that week that members are voting on.

weekPage.group.live.description: Heading of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: changes from that week that were approved and are now part of the running project.

weekPage.group.requests.description: Heading of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: requests (asks for something to be built or fixed) filed in that week.

weekPage.group.worked.description: Heading of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: requests and changes from that week that somebody is still working on.

weekPage.group.showAll_one.description: Button under the first few rows of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: shows every row of that group. {{count}} is how many rows the group has.

weekPage.group.showAll_other.description: Button under the first few rows of a group on a week's page in a project's Workshop tab: shows every row of that group. {{count}} is how many rows the group has.

sidePanel.label.description: Accessible name of the panel that opens beside the lists on a project's Workshop tab on a wide window: it holds the page of the request, change or vote whose row was pressed.

sidePanel.openAsPage.description: Button at the top of the panel beside a project's Workshop lists: closes the panel and opens the same request, change or vote as a full page. Open is a verb.

workRow.name.change.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "Change · evan · for #4455". A noun: one proposed change to the project that has no number yet.

workRow.name.changeNumbered.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "PR 4456 · evan · for #4455 · 4m ago". PR abbreviates pull request: one proposed change to the project. {{number}} is its number.

workRow.name.request.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "Request · evan · 8h ago". A noun: something a person asked to have built or fixed, shown without a number.

workRow.name.requestNumbered.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "#4417 · evan · 8h ago": a request (something a person asked to have built or fixed), named by its number alone. {{number}} is that number.

workRow.name.vote.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "Vote · evan". A noun: a proposal about the project's rules or settings that members vote on, shown without a number.

workRow.name.voteNumbered.description: What a row is, at the start of the line under its title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "Vote #7 · evan". A noun: a proposal about the project's rules or settings that members vote on. {{number}} is its number.

workRow.numbers.pair.description: Joins request numbers into a list in the line under a row's title in a project's lists of work, before the last one is added. {{first}} is the numbers so far and {{second}} the next, each written like #4455. Only the separator is translated.

workRow.numbers.last.description: Ends a list of request numbers in the line under a row's title in a project's lists of work, for example "#4455 and #4452" or "#1, #2 and #3". {{first}} is every number but the last, already joined, and {{last}} the last one.

workRow.for_one.description: One fact in the line under a change's title in a project's lists of work: the request this change was made for. {{requests}} is that request's number, for example #4455. {{count}} is how many requests there are and only picks the plural form.

workRow.for_other.description: One fact in the line under a change's title in a project's lists of work: the requests this change was made for. {{requests}} is the list of their numbers, for example "#4455 and #4452". {{count}} is how many requests there are and only picks the plural form.

workRow.closed_one.description: One fact in the line under a live change's title in a project's lists of work: the request this change settled when it went live. A past-tense verb; the change closed it. {{requests}} is that request's number, for example #4455. {{count}} is how many requests there are and only picks the plural form.

workRow.closed_other.description: One fact in the line under a live change's title in a project's lists of work: the requests this change settled when it went live. A past-tense verb; the change closed them. {{requests}} is the list of their numbers, for example "#4455 and #4452". {{count}} is how many requests there are and only picks the plural form.

workRow.facts.pair.description: Joins the short independent facts of the line under a row's title in a project's lists of work (the Workshop tab's lists and All items' board), for example "PR 4456 · evan · for #4455 · 4m ago". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the separator between them is translated.

workRow.replies_one.description: One fact on a Workshop row's line, after who made it: how many comments the item has. {{count}} is that number.

workRow.replies_other.description: One fact on a Workshop row's line, after who made it: how many comments the item has. {{count}} is that number.

needsYou.fact.approvals_one.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet: how many Yes votes a change has ({{yes}}) out of how many it needs to be approved ({{count}}).

needsYou.fact.approvals_other.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet: how many Yes votes a change has ({{yes}}) out of how many it needs to be approved ({{count}}).

needsYou.fact.yes_one.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed: how many people have voted Yes on the change so far.

needsYou.fact.yes_other.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed: how many people have voted Yes on the change so far.

needsYou.fact.no_one.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed: how many people have voted No on the change so far.

needsYou.fact.no_other.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed: how many people have voted No on the change so far.
