needsYou.fact.yourYesPutsItLive.description: On the line of facts under a Needs-you card's caption, after its approval count ("0 of 1 approval · your yes puts it live"), when exactly one more Yes meets the change's rule and the viewer's Yes counts. Lower case: it continues the line.

needsYou.fact.codeMissing.description: Red fact on the line under a Needs-you card's caption, after its approval count: the proposed change's code (its branch) did not come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub, so it cannot go live until the code is back. Votes on it are still recorded.

needsYou.fact.codeMissingTitle.text: This proposal’s code didn’t come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub. Its creator can submit it again, or Homeroom restores it when GitHub’s copy of the code arrives.
needsYou.fact.codeMissingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Code missing" fact on a Needs-you card. GitHub is a product name; Homeroom is the product's own name. "GitHub's copy of the code" is the export of the old repositories that GitHub is sending to Homeroom. "Submit it again" means put the same change up again.

needsYou.answered.votedYes.description: Confirmation at the top of an item in the Needs you feed once this person has voted Yes on the change. A hint on how to reach the next item follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.answered.votedNo.description: Confirmation at the top of an item in the Needs you feed once this person has voted No on the change. A hint on how to reach the next item follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.answered.approved.description: Confirmation at the top of an item in the Needs you feed once this person has approved the change, on a project that is just theirs. A hint on how to reach the next item follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.answered.notApproved.description: Confirmation at the top of an item in the Needs you feed once this person has declined the change, on a project that is just theirs. A hint on how to reach the next item follows it after a middle dot. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.fact.youVotedYes.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet, once this person has voted Yes on the change.

needsYou.fact.youVotedNo.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet, once this person has voted No on the change.

needsYou.fact.youApproved.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet, once this person has approved the change on a project that is just theirs.

needsYou.fact.youDidNotApprove.description: Fact at the foot of an item in the Needs you feed and on its Description sheet, once this person has declined the change on a project that is just theirs.

needsYou.vote.yes.description: Label of the Yes side of the vote switch on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, used when the item carries no label of its own.

needsYou.vote.no.description: Label of the No side of the vote switch on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, used when the item carries no label of its own.

needsYou.voteSub.approved.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's, once they have approved the change.

needsYou.voteSub.approvedState.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's, once they have approved the change. {{state}} is the change's status as its card says it, for example "Checks failing", without a full stop.

needsYou.voteSub.notApproved.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's, once they have declined the change.

needsYou.voteSub.notApprovedState.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's, once they have declined the change. {{state}} is the change's status as its card says it, for example "Checks failing", without a full stop.

needsYou.voteSub.waiting.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's: the change needs only their approval.

needsYou.voteSub.waitingState.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet, on a project that is just this person's: the change needs only their approval. {{state}} is the change's status as its card says it, for example "Checks failing", without a full stop.

needsYou.voteSub.nobody.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet when the change has no votes.

needsYou.voteSub.counts.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet: how many people voted Yes ({{yes}}) and how many voted No ({{no}}) on the change.

needsYou.voteSub.ofNeeded_one.text: {{count}} of {{needed}} have said yes so far.
needsYou.voteSub.ofNeeded_one.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet: how many people have voted Yes ({{count}}) out of how many Yes votes the change needs ({{needed}}).

needsYou.voteSub.ofNeeded_other.text: {{count}} of {{needed}} have said yes so far.
needsYou.voteSub.ofNeeded_other.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet: how many people have voted Yes ({{count}}) out of how many Yes votes the change needs ({{needed}}).

needsYou.voteSub.ofNeededState_one.text: {{count}} of {{needed}} have said yes so far. {{state}}.
needsYou.voteSub.ofNeededState_one.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet: how many people have voted Yes ({{count}}) out of how many Yes votes the change needs ({{needed}}). {{state}} is the change's status as its card says it, for example "Checks failing", without a full stop.

needsYou.voteSub.ofNeededState_other.text: {{count}} of {{needed}} have said yes so far. {{state}}.
needsYou.voteSub.ofNeededState_other.description: Line under the question on the Needs you feed's vote sheet: how many people have voted Yes ({{count}}) out of how many Yes votes the change needs ({{needed}}). {{state}} is the change's status as its card says it, for example "Checks failing", without a full stop.

shots.switch.label.description: Accessible name of the two-button switch over a change's screenshots in the Needs you feed: picks the screenshot taken before the change or the one taken after it.

shots.switch.before.description: Button of the switch over a change's screenshots in the Needs you feed: shows the screen as it was before the change.

shots.switch.after.description: Button of the switch over a change's screenshots in the Needs you feed: shows the screen as it is after the change.

shots.only.before.description: Label over a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed when only the screenshot from before the change exists.

shots.only.after.description: Label over a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed when only the screenshot from after the change exists.

shots.fullPage.description: Button over a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed: opens the full before and after comparison in an overlay. Keep the arrow.

shots.fullPageCropped.description: Button over a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed when the picture is cropped to the part that changed: says so, and opens the full before and after comparison in an overlay. Keep the arrow.

shots.alt.before.description: Alternative text of a screenshot in the Needs you feed: the screen as it was before the proposed change.

shots.alt.after.description: Alternative text of a screenshot in the Needs you feed: the screen as it is after the proposed change.

shots.size.phone.description: Label over a change's screenshots in the Needs you feed: the screenshots were taken at a phone's screen size.

shots.flip.toBefore.description: Accessible name of a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed while it shows the screen after the change: pressing the picture switches to the one from before.

shots.flip.toAfter.description: Accessible name of a change's screenshot in the Needs you feed while it shows the screen before the change: pressing the picture switches to the one from after.

needsYou.by.botName.description: Name shown as the author of a change in the Needs you feed when Homeroom's own building agent made it. A name: Homeroom is the product's name.

needsYou.by.at.description: The by-line over a Needs-you card's title, and at the top of its comments panel: who submitted the change, then how long ago. <0> is the name in bold; {{when}} is a short age such as "2h ago".

needsYou.by.anonymous.description: By-line over a change in the Needs you feed when its author is not known: it was put up for a vote. Past participle of the verb.

needsYou.by.anonymousAgo.description: By-line over a change in the Needs you feed when its author is not known: it was put up for a vote, and when. {{when}} is how long ago, already written out, for example "3d ago".

needsYou.next.wide.text: press ↓ or scroll for the next
needsYou.next.wide.description: Hint on an answered item in the Needs you feed on a wide window: how to move to the next item. It follows the confirmation ("Voted yes") after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. ↓ is the down arrow key. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.next.phone.description: Hint on an answered item in the Needs you feed on a phone: how to move to the next item. It follows the confirmation ("Voted yes") after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. It is one complete fact in a line of independent facts joined by the separator message project:facts.pair; it is not a clause of the fact beside it.

needsYou.eyebrow.groupDecision.text: Group decision · Waiting for your approval
needsYou.eyebrow.groupDecision.description: Small label at the top of an item in the Needs you feed: the item is a decision about the project itself (a rename, a setting, closing a request) and this person has not voted on it yet.

needsYou.eyebrow.change.description: Small label at the top of an item in the Needs you feed: the item is a proposed change to the app and this person has not voted on it yet. Change is a noun.

needsYou.eyebrow.changeAdvisory.description: Small label at the top of an item in the Needs you feed: the item is a proposed change whose outcome this person's vote does not decide — they are not an approver where only approvers decide, or outside every group the project's rules name. Their vote is recorded but does not affect the result. Change is a noun.

needsYou.eyebrow.ballot.text: Pick one · Changes for one request
needsYou.eyebrow.ballot.description: Small label at the top of an item in the Needs you feed: two or more changes (or a change and a proposal to close it) compete for one request, and this person has not picked one yet.

needsYou.eyebrow.botQuestion.description: Small label at the top of an item in the Needs you feed: a question Homeroom bot asked this person about their request, still unanswered.

needsYou.previousItem.description: Accessible name of the small up arrow at the top of an item in the Needs you feed on a phone: goes back to the item before.

needsYou.noSummary.change.text: No plain-language summary was written for this change.
needsYou.noSummary.change.description: Shown under a proposed change's title in the Needs you feed when it has no summary.

needsYou.caption.more.description: Small button at the end of the two-line summary in a Needs-you card's caption: grows the caption over the card's picture, with the whole description, what changes and what it touches. Lower case, as on a short video's caption.

needsYou.caption.less.description: Small button under a Needs-you card's opened caption: folds it back to two lines over the picture. Lower case, as on a short video's caption.

needsYou.caption.whatChanges.description: Small heading in a Needs-you card's opened caption, over the numbered list of what the change does on screen; the numbers match the outlines on its picture.

needsYou.swipe.yes.description: Word that fades in on an item in the Needs you feed while it is dragged to the right on a phone: letting go votes Yes on the change.

needsYou.swipe.no.description: Word that fades in on an item in the Needs you feed while it is dragged to the left on a phone: letting go votes No on the change.

needsYou.swipe.approve.description: Word that fades in on an item in the Needs you feed while it is dragged to the right on a phone, on a project that is just this person's: letting go approves the change. A verb.

needsYou.swipe.dontApprove.description: Words that fade in on an item in the Needs you feed while it is dragged to the left on a phone, on a project that is just this person's: letting go declines the change.

needsYou.end.forNow.description: Headline of the card at the end of the Needs-you feed when the viewer went past some decisions without answering them; they are still in the feed above.

needsYou.end.caughtUp.description: Headline of the card at the end of the Needs-you feed when the viewer answered everything that was waiting on them, or nothing was.

needsYou.end.reviewedAll_one.text: You reviewed the {{count}} change that was waiting on you.
needsYou.end.reviewedAll_one.description: Line under "All caught up" at the end of the Needs-you feed: the viewer voted on the one change that was waiting on them this time.

needsYou.end.reviewedAll_other.text: You reviewed all {{count}} changes that were waiting on you.
needsYou.end.reviewedAll_other.description: Line under "All caught up" at the end of the Needs-you feed: the viewer voted on every change that was waiting on them this time.

needsYou.end.reviewedSome_one.text: You reviewed {{done}} of the {{count}} change that was waiting on you.
needsYou.end.reviewedSome_one.description: Line under "That's it for now" at the end of the Needs-you feed: how many of the changes waiting on the viewer they voted on this time. {{done}} is how many, {{count}} how many there were.

needsYou.end.reviewedSome_other.text: You reviewed {{done}} of {{count}} changes that were waiting on you.
needsYou.end.reviewedSome_other.description: Line under "That's it for now" at the end of the Needs-you feed: how many of the changes waiting on the viewer they voted on this time. {{done}} is how many, {{count}} how many there were.

needsYou.end.skipped_one.text: You skipped {{count}}. It stays above if you change your mind.
needsYou.end.skipped_one.description: Sentences on the card after the last item of the Needs you feed: how many items this person passed without answering. They are still in the feed, above this card.

needsYou.end.skipped_other.text: You skipped {{count}}. They stay above if you change your mind.
needsYou.end.skipped_other.description: Sentences on the card after the last item of the Needs you feed: how many items this person passed without answering. They are still in the feed, above this card.

needsYou.end.allAnswered.text: Every change you can vote on has your answer.
needsYou.end.allAnswered.description: Line under "All caught up" at the end of the Needs-you feed when nothing was waiting on the viewer's vote.

needsYou.end.didHeading.description: Heading over the list, on the card at the end of the Needs-you feed, of each change the viewer voted on this time and where it stands now.

needsYou.end.status.live.description: Status beside a change in "What your votes did" at the end of the Needs-you feed: it went in and people are using it now.

needsYou.end.status.goingLive.description: Status beside a change in "What your votes did" at the end of the Needs-you feed: its rule is met and it is going in now.

needsYou.end.status.waiting_one.description: Status beside a change in "What your votes did" at the end of the Needs-you feed: how many more Yes votes its rule still needs.

needsYou.end.status.waiting_other.description: Status beside a change in "What your votes did" at the end of the Needs-you feed: how many more Yes votes its rule still needs.

needsYou.end.status.backToAuthor.description: Status beside a change in "What your votes did" at the end of the Needs-you feed, when the viewer voted no: their no and the line they wrote with it went to the change's author.

needsYou.end.overTheLine.text: Your yes put it over the line
needsYou.end.overTheLine.description: Headline of the note at the top of the card at the end of the Needs-you feed, when the viewer's Yes was the one that met a change's rule.

needsYou.end.overGoingLive.description: Line under "Your yes put it over the line" at the end of the Needs-you feed. {{title}} is the change's title.

needsYou.end.overLive.description: Line under "Your yes put it over the line" at the end of the Needs-you feed, once the change has gone live. {{title}} is the change's title.

needsYou.end.seeLive.description: Main button on the card at the end of a project's Needs-you feed: opens the project's Workshop, with what went live lately.

needsYou.end.backToHub.description: Second button on the card at the end of a project's Needs-you feed: back to the project's Hub.

needsYou.end.backToSkipped.text: Back to the first one you skipped
needsYou.end.backToSkipped.description: Button on the card after the last item of the Needs you feed: scrolls back up to the first item this person passed without answering.

needsYou.end.suggest.description: Quiet link on the card after the last item of a project's Needs you feed: opens the form for suggesting an improvement to this project.

needsYou.ask.reading.description: Placeholder answer in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed, shown in the conversation while the AI model is preparing its answer about the item.

needsYou.ask.failed.text: That did not go through. Try asking again.
needsYou.ask.failed.description: Shown in place of the answer in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed when the question could not be answered and the server gave no reason.

needsYou.ask.failedOffline.text: That did not go through. Check your connection and try again.
needsYou.ask.failedOffline.description: Shown in place of the answer in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed when the question could not be sent, most likely because the device is offline.

needsYou.ask.send.description: Accessible name of the round send button in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed: sends the question to the AI model. A verb.

needsYou.ask.private.text: Only you can see what you ask here.
needsYou.ask.private.description: Line at the top of the Ask tab on a Needs-you card's sheet: the questions and answers are the viewer's own and nobody else sees them.

needsYou.ask.hint.text: Ask what this changes, who it affects, or what happens if it goes in. Answered from what the platform knows about it.
needsYou.ask.hint.description: Text in the empty Ask sheet of the Needs you feed, before the first question: what can be asked and where the answer comes from. "Goes in" means is approved and merged.

needsYou.ask.noDetails.text: There are no details to ask about on this one.
needsYou.ask.noDetails.description: Text in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed when the item has nothing the AI model could answer from.

needsYou.ask.fieldLabel.description: Screen-reader label of the question field in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed. Ask is a verb; change is a noun.

needsYou.ask.placeholderNone.text: No details to ask about on this one
needsYou.ask.placeholderNone.description: Placeholder of the disabled question field in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed when the item has nothing to ask about.

needsYou.ask.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the question field in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed.

needsYou.ask.model.description: Screen-reader label of the menu in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed that picks which AI model answers.

needsYou.move.previous.description: Accessible name of the up arrow under the buttons beside an item in the Needs you feed on a wide window: goes to the item before.

needsYou.move.next.description: Accessible name of the down arrow under the buttons beside an item in the Needs you feed on a wide window: goes to the item after.

needsYou.rail.label.description: Accessible name of the column of buttons beside the item on screen in the Needs you feed (Vote, Skip, Comments, Ask, Try it, More).

needsYou.rail.endLabel.description: Accessible name of the column beside the last card of the Needs you feed, which holds only the arrows that move between items.

needsYou.rail.sending.description: Label of the Vote button beside an item in the Needs you feed while this person's vote is being sent.

needsYou.rail.approve.description: Button beside an item in the Needs you feed on a project that is just this person's: opens the sheet where they approve or decline the change. A verb.

needsYou.rail.vote.description: Button beside an item in the Needs you feed: opens the sheet where this person votes Yes or No on the change. A verb.

needsYou.rail.skip.description: Button beside an item in the Needs you feed: moves on to the next item without voting, leaving this one in the feed to vote on later. A verb.

needsYou.rail.skipThis.description: Accessible name of the Skip button beside an item in the Needs you feed: moves on without voting and leaves the change in the feed.

needsYou.rail.comments.description: Button beside an item in the Needs you feed, when the item has no comments yet: opens the sheet with the item's comments. With comments, the button shows their number instead.

needsYou.rail.commentsCount_one.description: What a screen reader says for the Comments button on the rail beside a Needs-you card, which shows only the number when there are comments.

needsYou.rail.commentsCount_other.description: What a screen reader says for the Comments button on the rail beside a Needs-you card, which shows only the number when there are comments.

needsYou.rail.ask.description: Button beside an item in the Needs you feed: opens a private question-and-answer box with an AI model about the item. A verb.

needsYou.rail.tryIt.description: Button beside a proposed change in the Needs you feed: opens the preview build of the app with the change applied, so it can be tried before voting.

needsYou.rail.moreActions.description: Accessible name of the three-dot button beside an item in the Needs you feed: opens the item's menu of further actions.

needsYou.rail.more.description: Visible label of the three-dot button beside an item in the Needs you feed: opens the item's menu of further actions.

needsYou.voteSheet.openToDecide.description: Link on the vote sheet of a group decision in the Needs you feed: opens the decision's own page, where its options are shown and voted on. Open is a verb.

needsYou.voteSheet.later.description: Button on the vote sheet of a group decision in the Needs you feed: closes the sheet without voting.

needsYou.voteSheet.keysApprove.text: Y approve · N don’t approve · Enter send · Esc close
needsYou.voteSheet.keysApprove.description: Keyboard hint at the bottom of the vote sheet in the Needs you feed, on a project that is just this person's. Y, N, Enter and Esc are the keys and must stay as written; translate only the words after each key.

needsYou.voteSheet.keysVote.text: Y yes · N no · Enter vote · Esc close
needsYou.voteSheet.keysVote.description: Keyboard hint at the bottom of the vote sheet in the Needs you feed. Y, N, Enter and Esc are the keys and must stay as written; translate only the words after each key (vote is a verb).

needsYou.keys.move.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed on a wide window: the arrow keys move between items. <0></0> and <1></1> draw the two keys; keep them and the arrows as written.

needsYou.keys.vote.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed: the V key opens the vote sheet. <0></0> draws the key; keep the letter V. Vote is a verb.

needsYou.keys.ask.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed: the A key opens the Ask sheet, a private question box about the item. <0></0> draws the key; keep the letter A. Ask is a verb.

needsYou.keys.comments.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed: the C key opens the item's comments. <0></0> draws the key; keep the letter C.

needsYou.keys.tryIt.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed: the T key opens the preview build of the app with the change applied. <0></0> draws the key; keep the letter T.

needsYou.keys.more.description: Entry in the list of keyboard shortcuts under the Needs you feed: the M key opens the item's menu of further actions. <0></0> draws the key; keep the letter M.

needsYou.comments.none.description: Text in the Comments sheet of the Needs you feed when the item has no comments and no thread to post in.

needsYou.talk.dialog.description: What a screen reader calls the sheet (a panel beside the card on a wide window) that holds a Needs-you card's comments and its Ask tab.

needsYou.talk.tabs.description: What a screen reader calls the two tabs at the top of a Needs-you card's comments sheet: Comments and Ask.

needsYou.talk.comments.description: Tab on a Needs-you card's sheet with what people have said about the change, when nobody has said anything yet.

needsYou.talk.commentsCount_one.description: Tab on a Needs-you card's sheet with what people have said about the change. <0> is the number of comments, drawn quieter.

needsYou.talk.commentsCount_other.description: Tab on a Needs-you card's sheet with what people have said about the change. <0> is the number of comments, drawn quieter.

needsYou.talk.ask.description: Tab on a Needs-you card's sheet where the viewer asks a model a private question about the change. This is a direct question to a model, not Homeroom bot.

needsYou.rail.votedYes.description: Label of the Vote button beside an item in the Needs you feed once this person has voted Yes on the change; the button then shows a check mark.

needsYou.rail.votedNo.description: Label of the Vote button beside an item in the Needs you feed once this person has voted No on the change; the button then shows a check mark.

needsYou.rail.approved.description: Label of the Approve button beside an item in the Needs you feed once this person has approved the change, on a project that is just theirs.

needsYou.rail.notApproved.description: Label of the Approve button beside an item in the Needs you feed once this person has declined the change, on a project that is just theirs.

needsYou.ask.placeholderReading.description: Placeholder of the disabled question field in the Ask sheet of the Needs you feed while the AI model is preparing its answer.

pageBack.backTo.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the round back arrow at the top of a page inside a project (its Workshop, Needs you, All items, the plan) and of a project's discussion channel. {{place}} is where it goes back to: the project's name, or the name of the tab above, such as Hub.

ask.failed.text: That did not go through. Try asking again.
ask.failed.description: Error shown under a proposal on the Needs you feed when a question the person asked the AI about that proposal could not be answered and the server gave no reason of its own.

plan.step.description: Line under the title of the read-only plan page for a project's first version: how far the assistant's work on it has come. {{step}} is the current step's number and {{total}} how many steps there are, for example Step 3 of 7.

plan.decides.named.description: Line at the foot of the read-only plan page for a project's first version, telling a member who may approve the plan. {{username}} is the username of the person who started the project.

plan.decides.starter.text: The person who started it decides on this plan.
plan.decides.starter.description: Line at the foot of the read-only plan page for a project's first version, when the name of the person who started the project is not known. "It" is the project.

plan.chosen.named.text: {{username}} chose this plan. Once it’s live, anyone here can suggest changes.
plan.chosen.named.description: Line on the read-only plan page of a project's first version while the plan is being built or tested: its maker already chose it. {{username}} is the maker's username. "Live" means built and running.

plan.chosen.starter.text: The person who started it chose this plan. Once it’s live, anyone here can suggest changes.
plan.chosen.starter.description: Line on the read-only plan page of a project's first version while the plan is being built or tested, when the maker's name is not known. "It" is the project. "Live" means built and running.

plan.backHub.description: Name of the place the back arrow on the read-only plan page returns to: the project's Hub tab. It fills the place in "Back to Hub".

plan.botNameBadge.description: Author's name at the top of the read-only plan page, beside the assistant's picture, with a small badge after it. "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant, which wrote the plan; keep "Homeroom". <0></0> is the badge marking the author as an AI assistant rather than a person.

plan.title.description: Heading of the read-only plan page. "My" is Homeroom bot, the assistant, speaking: it is the plan the assistant wrote for the project's first version. {{project}} is the project's name.

plan.linesLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of the plan's lines, on the read-only plan page and in the plan sheet a member opens from the App tab while the first version is built. {{project}} is the project's name.

plan.talk.description: Button at the foot of the read-only plan page: opens the project's #general channel so a member can say something about the plan. "#general" is the name of that channel; keep it as written.

discussion.label.description: Accessible name of the Discussion tab's content on a project's page: the project's chat channel. {{project}} is the project's name.

discussion.none.text: This project has no discussion you can read.
discussion.none.description: Shown on a project's Discussion tab in place of the chat when this person is not allowed to read the project's channel.

discussion.closeThread.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the X button on the panel of replies to one message, beside a project's discussion. Close is a verb: it hides the panel of replies.

invite.from.isMaking.text: {{name}} is making it and invited you
invite.from.isMaking.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, while the project's first version is still being built. {{name}} is the display name of the person who started the project and sent the invite; "it" is the project.

invite.from.made.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button. {{name}} is the display name of the person who started the project and sent the invite; "it" is the project.

invite.from.invited.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, when the inviter did not start the project. {{username}} is the inviter's username; keep the @ before it.

invite.from.unnamed.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, when who sent the invite is not known.

invite.dead.expired.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link's time limit ran out in the meantime.

invite.dead.revoked.text: That invite link was turned off.
invite.dead.revoked.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the person who made the link has cancelled it.

invite.dead.usedUp.text: That invite link has been used as many times as it allows.
invite.dead.usedUp.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link's limit on how many people may use it has been reached.

invite.dead.paused.text: This invite link is paused. Ask the person who shared it for a new one.
invite.dead.paused.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link stopped letting people in for now because a lot of people joined through it in one day.

invite.dead.unknown.text: That invite link does not work.
invite.dead.unknown.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link is not one Homeroom knows.

invite.previewOnly.text: This is a preview of an invite, so nothing was joined.
invite.previewOnly.description: Toast after pressing Join on a demonstration copy of an invited person's view of a project's page, which follows no real invite link.

invite.joinFailed.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when joining failed for a reason the server did not explain or the request did not get through.

invite.usernameFirst.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the person has no username yet and a public community requires one. Shown only when the server sent no sentence of its own.

invite.joined.description: Toast shown once a person has joined a community through an invite link.

hub.channel.unread_one.description: Small badge in the head of the Discussion card: how many messages in the project's channel are unread. {{shown}} is that number as displayed, capped as 99+; the plural form follows the real count.

hub.channel.unread_other.description: Small badge in the head of the Discussion card: how many messages in the project's channel are unread. {{shown}} is that number as displayed, capped as 99+; the plural form follows the real count.

hub.channel.empty.description: Second line of the Discussion row in the "For you" card on a project's hub, when nobody has said anything in the project's channel yet. The row opens the channel.

hub.firstVersion.review.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for the person who started the project: opens their chat with Homeroom bot, where the plan for the first version waits for their go-ahead.

hub.firstVersion.answer.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for the person who started the project: opens their chat with Homeroom bot, which has asked them a question before it can go on building.

hub.firstVersion.tryIt.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub once the first version is built and up for approval: opens that version so the person can use it before approving. "It" is the app.

hub.firstVersion.openApp.description: Button on the first-version card of a project's Hub once the first version is live. Open is a verb: goes to the running app.

hub.firstVersion.tryAgain.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for the person who started the project, when Homeroom bot's build of the first version stopped before the app went live: opens the build's conversation in their chat with Homeroom bot, where they can start it again.

hub.firstVersion.seePlan.description: Quiet link on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for a member who did not start the project: opens the plan for the first version to read, without being able to answer it.

hub.firstLook.text.text: Drawn from your answers. We'll tell you when the working app is live.
hub.firstLook.text.description: Line on a project's Hub card while its first version is being built, shown to the person who started the project, under the project's name and how far the build has got: the small picture beside it was drawn from the answers the person gave when they made the project, the real app is still being built, and they will be told once it is published ("live").

hub.firstLook.watch.description: Button on a project's Hub card while its first version is being built, beside the first look at it: opens the project's App tab, where the app can be seen taking shape while the assistant called Homeroom bot builds it. "It" is the app; Homeroom bot is a name.

hub.firstLook.alt.text: The first look at {{app}}'s main screen
hub.firstLook.alt.description: Description, for screen readers, of the small picture on the first-look card of a project's Hub: a drawing of the app's main screen, made before the app was built. {{app}} is the project's name.

hub.firstLook.open.text: Open your chat with Homeroom bot
hub.firstLook.open.description: Name, for screen readers, of the first-look card on a project's Hub, for the person who started the project: a tap on its picture or its words opens their chat with the assistant called Homeroom bot, where the build is reported. Homeroom bot is a name.

hub.needs.title.description: Heading of the card on a project's Hub that leads to the Needs you tab: the proposals waiting for this person's vote.

hub.needs.toVote_one.description: Beside the heading of the Needs you card on a project's Hub: how many proposals this person has not yet looked at and still has to vote on.

hub.needs.toVote_other.description: Beside the heading of the Needs you card on a project's Hub: how many proposals this person has not yet looked at and still has to vote on.

hub.needs.skipped_one.text: {{count}} vote you skipped is still open
hub.needs.skipped_one.description: Line on the Needs you card of a project's Hub when every proposal waiting for this person's vote is one they already swiped past without voting: how many of those can still be voted on.

hub.needs.skipped_other.text: {{count}} votes you skipped are still open
hub.needs.skipped_other.description: Line on the Needs you card of a project's Hub when every proposal waiting for this person's vote is one they already swiped past without voting: how many of those can still be voted on.

hub.needs.joinToVote.description: Note under the Needs you card of a project's Hub for a person who is not a member of the community: they must join it before they can vote on the proposals. "These" are the proposals.

hub.needs.none.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote.

hub.needs.noneButRequests_one.text: Nothing more to vote on · <0>{{count}} request nobody has picked up</0>
hub.needs.noneButRequests_one.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote but some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The part in <0></0> is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.noneButRequests_other.text: Nothing more to vote on · <0>{{count}} requests nobody has picked up</0>
hub.needs.noneButRequests_other.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote but some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The part in <0></0> is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.requestsAlone_one.description: Quiet line on the Hub of a project that has only one person in it, when some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The whole line, inside <0></0>, is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.requestsAlone_other.description: Quiet line on the Hub of a project that has only one person in it, when some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The whole line, inside <0></0>, is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.people.active_one.description: Top of a project's Hub, beside the faces of the people active there: how many people took part in the project in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted).

hub.people.active_other.description: Top of a project's Hub, beside the faces of the people active there: how many people took part in the project in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted).

hub.people.namesAndMore_one.description: Line under "40 active this week" at the top of a project's Hub. {{names}} is a list of up to five usernames of people active this week, already joined with commas; {{count}} is how many more people were active who are not named.

hub.people.namesAndMore_other.description: Line under "40 active this week" at the top of a project's Hub. {{names}} is a list of up to five usernames of people active this week, already joined with commas; {{count}} is how many more people were active who are not named.

hub.people.moreFaces_one.description: Last circle in the row of faces at the top of a project's Hub: how many more people were active this week than the faces shown. Keep it as short as a plus sign and a number.

hub.people.moreFaces_other.description: Last circle in the row of faces at the top of a project's Hub: how many more people were active this week than the faces shown. Keep it as short as a plus sign and a number.

hub.topics.title.description: On a phone, small heading over the card on a project's Hub that lists the project's topics, each a channel of its own, one row a topic, under the For you card. Pressing a row opens that topic's channel.

hub.forYou.title.description: Small heading over the card of what on a project is this person's: the votes they owe, their own work and the project's discussion, on the project's Hub.

hub.forYou.needs.firstAndMore_one.description: Second line of the Needs you row on a project's Hub: the title of the first change waiting on this person's vote, then how many more are waiting. {{title}} is that change's title.

hub.forYou.needs.firstAndMore_other.description: Second line of the Needs you row on a project's Hub: the title of the first change waiting on this person's vote, then how many more are waiting. {{title}} is that change's title.

hub.forYou.discussion.title.description: Title of the row that opens a project's discussion on its Hub. <0></0> draws the channel's name in a lighter weight; {{handle}} is the channel's name without the #, for example general.

hub.forYou.discussion.lastBy.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub: the last message in the channel, who wrote it and how long ago. {{username}} is the writer, {{message}} the message itself, {{ago}} a time such as "4h ago". <0> wraps the part that is cut short when the line is too long, <1> the time, which is always shown whole.

hub.forYou.discussion.last.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the last message in the channel has no writer to name: the message and how long ago it was sent. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago". <0> wraps the message, which is cut short when the line is too long, <1> the time, which is always shown whole.

hub.forYou.discussion.postedBy.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the newest message in the channel has no words to quote (only a picture or a file): who sent it and how long ago. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago".

hub.forYou.discussion.posted.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the newest message in the channel has no words to quote and no writer to name: how long ago it was sent. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago".

hub.recent.title.description: Small heading over the cards of the last few changes that went live, on a project's Hub.

hub.recent.all.description: Link beside the Recently live heading on a project's Hub: opens the project's Workshop, where everything that went live is listed week by week.

hub.recent.byAgo.description: Line under a change's title in Recently live on a project's Hub: who made the change and how long ago it went live. {{who}} is a username or "Homeroom bot"; {{ago}} a time such as "1h ago".

hub.recent.byGoing.description: Line under a change's title in Recently live on a project's Hub, for a change that has merged and is still on its way to the live app. {{who}} is a username or "Homeroom bot".

hub.recent.going.description: Line under a change's title in Recently live on a project's Hub, for a change that has merged and is still on its way to the live app, when there is no maker to name.

hub.recent.own.today.description: Under the app's own name on the one card in the "Recently live" section of a project's hub, shown before any change to the app has gone live: the app itself went live today. The card opens the app.

hub.recent.own.since.description: Under the app's own name on the one card in the "Recently live" section of a project's hub, shown before any change to the app has gone live: the day the app went live. {{date}} is a day in words, for example "October 12" or "October 12, 2025". The card opens the app.

communityCard.rule.you.text: A change goes live when you approve it.
communityCard.rule.you.description: The approval rule of a project that is just this person's own (audience "Just you"): they are its only approver. Read out by a screen reader as the name of the three-step drawing under Approval rules on the project's Workshop tab. A change is one proposed change to the project.

communityCard.rule.fixed_one.text: A change goes live once {{count}} member approves it.
communityCard.rule.fixed_one.description: The approval rule of a project whose settings fix the number of approvals a change needs, read out by a screen reader as the name of the three-step drawing under Approval rules on the project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is that number of members.

communityCard.rule.fixed_other.text: A change goes live once {{count}} members approve it.
communityCard.rule.fixed_other.description: The approval rule of a project whose settings fix the number of approvals a change needs, read out by a screen reader as the name of the three-step drawing under Approval rules on the project's Workshop tab. {{count}} is that number of members.

communityCard.rule.approvers.some_one.text: A change goes live when {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers says yes.
communityCard.rule.approvers.some_one.description: The approval rule of a project where only invited approvers vote on changes, read out by a screen reader as the name of the three-step drawing under Approval rules on the project's Workshop tab. Used when fewer than all of them are needed: {{count}} is how many must agree (it sets the plural form) and {{total}} how many there are.

communityCard.rule.approvers.some_other.text: A change goes live when {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers say yes.

communityCard.audience.justYou.description: Name of the audience of a project only its maker is in, used as the project's audience line when the server sent no label. It is one of the three audience names, beside Private community and Public community.

communityCard.audience.justYouSoFar.description: Who a project is for, shown at the top of its Hub to the one person in it while nobody else has joined, with an Invite button beside it. "Just you" is the name of that audience (beside Private community and Public community); "so far" says it can grow.

communityCard.audience.withMembers_one.description: One-line summary of who a project is for and how many people are in it. {{audience}} is the audience's name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.audience.withMembers_other.description: One-line summary of who a project is for and how many people are in it. {{audience}} is the audience's name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.audienceChange.toPublic.text: Making it a public community is waiting for approval
communityCard.audienceChange.toPublic.description: Link line at the foot of a project's Hub header while a proposal to make the project a public community is up for a vote; an arrow follows and it opens that proposal. "It" is the project.

communityCard.audienceChange.toPrivate.text: Making it a private community is waiting for approval
communityCard.audienceChange.toPrivate.description: Link line at the foot of a project's Hub header while a proposal to make the project a private community is up for a vote; an arrow follows and it opens that proposal. "It" is the project.

communityCard.audienceChange.other.text: A change to who it is for is waiting for approval
communityCard.audienceChange.other.description: Link line at the foot of a project's Hub header while a proposal that changes the project's audience in some other way is up for a vote; an arrow follows and it opens that proposal. "It" is the project.

communityCard.audienceChange.failed.text: That did not go through. Try again.
communityCard.audienceChange.failed.description: Error shown when proposing to make a project public or private failed and the server gave no reason of its own: as a toast after the confirm dialog, or under the question in the Make it public popup.

communityCard.people.members_one.description: Line beside the members' faces at the top of a project's Hub, when the audience's name is not known: how many members the community has.

communityCard.people.members_other.description: Line beside the members' faces at the top of a project's Hub, when the audience's name is not known: how many members the community has.

communityCard.people.audienceMembers_one.description: Line beside the members' faces at the top of a project's Hub: who the community is for, then how many members it has. <0></0> draws the audience's name in bold after a small icon. {{audience}} is that name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.people.audienceMembers_oth.description: Line beside the members' faces at the top of a project's Hub: who the community is for, then how many members it has. <0></0> draws the audience's name in bold after a small icon. {{audience}} is that name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.makePublic.question.description: Question asked before proposing to make a private project public: the title of the confirm dialog from the project's ⋯ menu, and the question in the popup under the "Make it public" button. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.makePublic.explain.text: Anyone can find it on Discover, join, and propose changes. Members vote on this first, and it applies once it merges.
communityCard.makePublic.explain.description: Explanation under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?". "It" is the project; Discover is the name of the screen for finding apps and communities. "This" is the proposal to make it public, which is put to a vote and takes effect once it is merged.

communityCard.makePublic.propose.description: Confirming button under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?": puts the change up as a proposal for the members to vote on. "It" is the project.

communityCard.makePublic.notNow.description: Declining button under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?": closes it and leaves the project as it is.

communityCard.share.title.description: Heading of a card at the foot of the Hub of a project only its maker is in, offering to invite people or make it public. Share is a verb; "it" is the project.

communityCard.lineage.madeFrom.gets.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub, on a version (a project made from another, the original), when it gets the original's changes to try and vote on. {{project}} is the original's name; the tagged name links to it. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

communityCard.lineage.madeFrom.doesNotGe.text: Made from <0>{{project}}</0> · Doesn’t get its updates
communityCard.lineage.madeFrom.doesNotGe.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub, on a version (a project made from another, the original), when it does not get the original's changes. {{project}} is the original's name; the tagged name links to it. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

communityCard.lineage.versions.count_one.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub, on a project others have made versions of (each a project of its own, made with Make your own), when none of them gets this project's updates. {{count}} is how many versions there are.

communityCard.lineage.versions.count_oth.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub, on a project others have made versions of (each a project of its own, made with Make your own), when none of them gets this project's updates. {{count}} is how many versions there are.

communityCard.lineage.versions.oneGetsUp.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub when one version of it has been made, and that version gets this project's changes to try and vote on. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

communityCard.lineage.versions.manyGetUp.description: Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub: {{versions}} is how many versions others have made of this project (always more than one here), and {{count}} how many of them get its changes to try and vote on. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

Line in the hero at the top of a project's hub: {{versions}} is how many versions others have made of this project (always more than one here), and {{count}} how many of them get its changes to try and vote on. Keep the middle dot as a separator.

communityCard.share.line.text: Invite people to make it a private community, or make it public so anyone can join.
communityCard.share.line.description: Text of the "Share it" card on the Hub of a project only its maker is in, above the Invite people and Make it public buttons. "It" is the project.

communityCard.share.lineBuilding.text: Invite people to follow along while it’s being built, or make it public so anyone can join.
communityCard.share.lineBuilding.description: Text of the "Share it" card on the Hub of a project only its maker is in, while Homeroom bot is still building the project's first version. "It" is the project.

communityCard.share.invite.description: Button on the "Share it" card: opens the pane that makes an invite link to the project.

communityCard.share.makePublic.description: Button on the "Share it" card: opens a small popup asking whether to propose making the project a public community. "It" is the project.

communityCard.share.sent_one.description: Starts the one line on the "Share it" card of a project that is just the person's own, once they have made an invite link for it that still works. Followed by who has joined and how long the link has left, for example "Invite link sent · nobody has joined yet · 7 days left".

communityCard.share.sent_other.description: Starts the one line on the "Share it" card of a project that is just the person's own, when more than one invite link for it still works. Followed by who has joined and how long the soonest link has left, for example "2 invite links sent · 1 joined · 3 days left".

communityCard.share.nobodyJoined.description: Part of the one line on the "Share it" card, after "Invite link sent": nobody has joined the project through the invite link yet. Lower case because it follows a separator in the middle of the line.

communityCard.share.joined_one.description: Part of the one line on the "Share it" card, after "Invite link sent": how many people have joined the project through the invite link.

communityCard.share.joined_other.description: Part of the one line on the "Share it" card, after "Invite link sent": how many people have joined the project through the invite link.

communityCard.share.daysLeft_one.description: Ends the one line on the "Share it" card: how many days the invite link still works, rounded. Lower case because it follows a separator in the middle of the line.

communityCard.share.daysLeft_other.description: Ends the one line on the "Share it" card: how many days the invite link still works, rounded. Lower case because it follows a separator in the middle of the line.

communityCard.share.expiresToday.description: Ends the one line on the "Share it" card when the invite link stops working in less than a day. Lower case because it follows a separator in the middle of the line.

communityCard.inviteCard.note.description: The inviter's personal note, shown in quotation marks under the line saying who invited the person, on a project's page opened from an invite link. {{note}} is text the inviter wrote; only the quotation marks are translated.

communityCard.inviteCard.join.description: Large main button at the top of a project's page opened from an invite link, and on the preview of a private community's invite: joins the community through that link. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.inviteCard.joinUnnamed.description: Large main button at the top of a project's page opened from an invite link, and on the preview of a private community's invite: joins the community through that link. Used when the community's name did not come with the link.

communityCard.join.button.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, for a person who is not a member: opens a small popup asking whether to join the community.

communityCard.join.question.description: Question in the small popup under the Join button at the top of a project's Hub, and that popup's accessible name. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.join.explain.text: Members start changes, file requests, vote and chat here.
communityCard.join.explain.description: Explanation under the question "Join {{project}}?": what a member of the community can do in the project. Changes are proposed changes to the project; requests are filed issues.

communityCard.join.answer.description: Confirming button under the question "Join {{project}}?": makes the person a member of the community.

communityCard.join.notNow.description: Declining button under the question "Join {{project}}?": closes the popup without joining.

communityCard.openApp.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, after a play icon. Open is a verb: goes to the running app.

communityCard.invite.button.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, for a member. A verb: opens the pane that makes an invite link to the community.

communityCard.invite.title.description: Tooltip of the Invite button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub.

topic.frame.resizeSpecPanel.description: Accessible name of the draggable divider between a proposal's or request's page and the plan reader docked beside it. A plan is the written description a change is built from.

topic.back.messages.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page when it was opened from a conversation: the name of the Messages screen it returns to. Shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.workshop.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page: the name of the project's Workshop tab (the build tab beside its Hub) that the chip returns to. A noun, shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.toMessages.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page that was opened from a conversation. Messages is the screen of the person's conversations.

topic.back.toWorkshop.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page. Workshop is the project's build tab, where its proposals and requests are listed.

topic.back.bot.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page when it was opened from the Homeroom bot tab's page: the name of that tab, which the chip returns to. Homeroom bot is the platform's builder bot (a name). Shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.toBot.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page that was opened from the Homeroom bot tab's page, which it returns to. Homeroom bot is the platform's builder bot (a name), and the tab is named for it.

topic.editor.title.description: Heading of the dialog where the author of a change rewrites the description people read before voting on it.

topic.editor.closeLabel.description: Accessible name of the X button that closes the edit-description dialog of a change without saving.

topic.editor.help.text: Explain the problem and what this change does. Markdown is supported.
topic.editor.help.description: Help line under the heading of the edit-description dialog of a change. Markdown is the name of a text formatting syntax; do not translate it.

topic.editor.restored.text: Your unsaved text was brought back from this device.
topic.editor.restored.description: Status line in the edit-description dialog of a change, shown when text the person typed before their sign-in ran out has been put back in the field from this device.

topic.editor.loading.description: Status line in the edit-description dialog of a change while the current description is being fetched.

topic.editor.fieldLabel.description: Label of the large text field in the edit-description dialog of a change. A noun: the text describing the change.

topic.editor.previewRegion.description: Accessible name of the area that shows the formatted description, in the edit-description dialog of a change, while Preview is on.

topic.editor.preview.description: Toggle button in the edit-description dialog of a change: shows the description as it will look once formatted, in place of the text field. A verb.

topic.editor.editText.description: Toggle button in the edit-description dialog of a change, shown while the formatted preview is on: goes back to the text field.

topic.editor.tooLong.text: Shorten the description before saving; none of your text has been removed.
topic.editor.tooLong.description: Alert in the edit-description dialog of a change when the text is over the length limit. Saving is disabled until it is shorter.

topic.editor.loadFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when the current description could not be fetched and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.editor.saveFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when saving was refused and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.editor.connectFailed.text: Could not connect. Your draft is kept; try saving again.
topic.editor.connectFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when the save request could not reach the server. The text the person typed is still in the field.

topic.editor.savedSyncIncomplete.text: Saved in Homeroom. Pull-request synchronization is incomplete. Save again to retry.
topic.editor.savedSyncIncomplete.description: Status line in the edit-description dialog of a change: the description was saved, but copying it to the change's pull request on GitHub failed. Homeroom is the product's name.

topic.editor.savedToast.description: Brief confirmation shown after the edit-description dialog of a change saved and closed.

topic.editor.reviewLatest.description: Button in the edit-description dialog of a change, shown when someone else saved a newer description while the person was editing: loads that newer text so the two can be compared.

topic.editor.latestTitle.description: Heading over the newer description somebody else saved, shown in the edit-description dialog of a change after a save conflict.

topic.editor.useLatest.description: Button under the newer description in the edit-description dialog of a change: replaces the person's draft with that newer saved text.

topic.editor.keepDraft.description: Button under the newer description in the edit-description dialog of a change: keeps what the person typed, so saving will overwrite the newer saved text.

topic.editor.save.description: Main button of the edit-description dialog of a change: saves the text as the change's description.

topic.editor.saving.description: Text of the main button in the edit-description dialog of a change while the description is being saved.

topic.editor.retrySync.description: Text of the main button in the edit-description dialog of a change after the description was saved but could not be copied to its pull request on GitHub: saves again to retry that copy. GitHub is a product name.

topic.check.advisory.description: Small lower-case tag on one automated check in a change's list of checks: this check's result is shown for information and does not block the change from going live.

topic.check.flaky.description: Small lower-case tag on one automated check in a change's list of checks: the check fails intermittently. {{percent}} is the share of its recorded runs that failed. Keep the dot and the percent sign.

topic.check.flakyTitle.text: Failed about {{percent}}% of its recorded runs
topic.check.flakyTitle.description: Hover text of the "flaky" tag on an automated check. {{percent}} is the share of that check's recorded runs that failed.

topic.check.whyItFailed.description: Link-like label at the right end of a failed automated check's row on a change's page: opens the reason the check failed. "It" is the check.

topic.check.passedOnRetry.description: Link-like label at the right end of an automated check's row on a change's page, for a check that failed once and passed when run again: opens the reason of the first failure.

topic.check.earlyBurst.description: Link-like label at the right end of an automated check's row on a change's page, for a check that failed in a burst of failures at the start of the test run and passed every time it was run again. Opens the explanation, which names a likely cause without excusing the change.

topic.check.freshLoad.description: Link-like label at the right end of a passing automated check's row on a change's page, for a check this change adds or changes that only passed after its page was loaded again from scratch. Opens advice on fixing the page's navigation.

topic.check.failed.description: Lower-case word shown as the reason of a failed automated check when the run recorded no reason. Describes the check.

topic.check.reasonOnPath.description: The opened reason of a failed automated check, followed by the page it ran on. {{reason}} is the recorded reason, or the word for "failed"; {{path}} is the address of the page inside the app, for example /settings. <0></0> dims the second part; keep the dot and the space before it inside the tag.

topic.check.unit.name.description: Name of one row in a change's list of automated checks: the app's own test suite, which its code comes with. Shown when that suite failed.

topic.check.unit.failedOf_one.description: At the end of the "The app's own tests" row in a change's list of checks: {{failed}} of the suite's {{total}} tests failed, both already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural.

topic.check.unit.failedOf_other.description: At the end of the "The app's own tests" row in a change's list of checks: {{failed}} of the suite's {{total}} tests failed, both already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural.

topic.check.unit.failed_one.description: At the end of the "The app's own tests" row in a change's list of checks, when the total is not known: {{failed}} of its tests failed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.check.unit.failed_other.description: At the end of the "The app's own tests" row in a change's list of checks, when the total is not known: {{failed}} of its tests failed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.check.unit.testsThatFailed_one.description: Small heading over the failing test in the "The app's own tests" row of a change's list of checks. {{count}} is how many tests are listed under it; English does not show it.

topic.check.unit.testsThatFailed_other.description: Small heading over the failing tests in the "The app's own tests" row of a change's list of checks. {{count}} is how many tests are listed under it; English does not show it.

topic.check.unit.said.description: Under one failing test's name in a change's list of checks: the message it failed with. {{said}} is that message as the app's code wrote it, usually in English.

topic.check.unit.fileLine.description: Under one failing test's name in a change's list of checks: where the test is. {{file}} is a file path in the app's code and {{line}} a line number in it.

topic.check.unit.showOutput.description: Link-like label that unfolds the raw output the app's failing tests printed, in a change's list of checks. It is technical text for whoever fixes the tests.

topic.check.showFullOutput.description: Link-like label that unfolds everything a failed automated check recorded besides its error line (console messages and test printouts), in a change's list of checks. The error line itself is already shown above it.

topic.check.unit.showMore_one.description: Link-like label that unfolds the other failing tests in the "The app's own tests" row of a change's list of checks, when exactly one more test failed. {{count}} is that number, always 1.

topic.check.unit.showMore_other.description: Link-like label that unfolds the other failing tests in the "The app's own tests" row of a change's list of checks. {{count}} is how many tests are folded away; the first failing test is already shown above it.

topic.checks.explain.title.description: Small heading over a plain explanation of why a change's automated checks failed, in its list of checks.

topic.checks.explain.source.text: Homeroom’s reading of the test output.
topic.checks.explain.source.description: Small note under the plain explanation of why a change's checks failed: the explanation was written by Homeroom (with AI) from the tests' technical output, so it may be imperfect. Homeroom is the product's name; do not translate it.

topic.checks.fixing.description: Text of the disabled Fix it button in a change's list of checks while the AI agent is fixing the checks that failed.

topic.checks.showPassing_one.description: Label that unfolds the list of automated checks that passed, in the checks box under a proposal. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.checks.showPassing_other.description: Label that unfolds the list of automated checks that passed, in the checks box under a proposal. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.checks.passNamesLoading.description: Line inside the unfolded list of passed automated checks on a change's page while their names are being fetched.

topic.checks.passNamesFailed.text: Could not load the passing checks. Close this and open it again to retry.
topic.checks.passNamesFailed.description: Line inside the unfolded list of passed automated checks on a change's page when their names could not be fetched. "This" is the fold the person just opened.

topic.ledger.passing_one.description: Small button on the checks row of a change's page that unfolds the automated checks that passed. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.ledger.passing_other.description: Small button on the checks row of a change's page that unfolds the automated checks that passed. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.build.seconds.description: How long one step of a change's preview build took, when under a minute, shown small after the step's name. {{seconds}} is a whole number; "s" abbreviates seconds.

topic.build.minutesSeconds.description: How long one step of a change's preview build took, when a minute or more, shown small after the step's name. {{minutes}} and {{seconds}} are whole numbers; "m" and "s" abbreviate minutes and seconds.

topic.roster.loading.description: Shown on the votes line of a proposal's page while the list of who voted is being fetched.

topic.roster.approved.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs, when no voter can be named. Describes the proposal.

topic.roster.approvedBy.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs. {{approvers}} is the list of people who voted Yes, already joined, for example "@maya ✓, @sam". <0></0> shows the first word bold in green.

topic.roster.approvedByWithNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs although some people voted No. {{approvers}} is the list of people who voted Yes and {{against}} the list who voted No, each already joined. <0></0> shows the first word bold in green; <1></1> dims the No part: keep the dot and the space before it inside that tag. "No" is the name of the vote against.

topic.roster.approvedWithNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs, when only the people who voted No can be named. {{against}} is that list, already joined. <0></0> shows the first word bold in green; <1></1> dims the No part: keep the dot and the space before it inside that tag.

topic.roster.waiting.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when nobody has voted either way.

topic.roster.waitingYes.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when only Yes votes were cast. {{yesLabel}} is the Yes side's label with its count, for example "Yes (2)", and {{yesNames}} the people who voted Yes, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <1></1> colours the label.

topic.roster.waitingYesNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when people voted both ways. {{yesLabel}} and {{noLabel}} are each side's label with its count, for example "Yes (2)" and "No (1)"; {{yesNames}} and {{noNames}} are the people on each side, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <1></1> and <2></2> colour the two labels.

topic.roster.waitingNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when only No votes were cast. {{noLabel}} is the No side's label with its count, for example "No (1)", and {{noNames}} the people who voted No, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <2></2> colours the label; keep its number.

topic.roster.reason.description: One line under a proposal's votes: a voter and the sentence they wrote with their vote, quoted. {{voter}} is the person's @name and {{reason}} their own words. Use the quotation marks of the language.

topic.help.howVotingWorks.description: Link at the right end of the votes line on a proposal's page: opens a short explanation of how proposals are voted on and go live.

topic.help.votingAndMerges.description: Accessible name and hover text of the round "?" button beside "How voting works" on a proposal's page: opens the same explanation. A merge is an approved change going into the project's code.

topic.steps.votingHelp.description: Accessible name and hover text of the round "?" button on the Votes step of a proposal's list of steps: opens a short explanation of voting. A merge is an approved change going into the project's code.

topic.steps.voteTally.description: The count of votes on the Votes step of a proposal. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes and {{no}} the number of No votes. Yes and No are the names of the two votes.

topic.about.title.description: Heading of the section under a proposal's or request's card that holds its description, used when the page gave no more specific heading. A noun-like heading, as in "About this change".

topic.about.whatChanges.description: Sub-heading over the plain-language summary of a proposal: what people using the app will notice once the change is live.

topic.about.technicalDetails.description: Label that unfolds the full technical description of a proposal (its pull-request text), under the plain-language summary.

topic.about.testing.title.description: Label that unfolds the instructions for trying a proposal out before voting on it.

topic.about.testing.recordedIn.description: Shown under "Testing instructions" on a proposal when the instructions exist only as a file in the project's code. {{path}} is that file's path.

topic.about.testing.none.text: No testing instructions have been added yet.
topic.about.testing.none.description: Shown under "Testing instructions" on a proposal that has none.

topic.hero.howItsBuilt.description: Label that unfolds the technical design part of a change's summary on the change's page, under the part written for the people deciding on it. "It" is the change.

topic.transcript.readOnly.description: Small lower-case tag on the fold that shows the chat in which a change was built: the chat can be read here but not continued.

topic.change.refreshFailed.description: Error at the top of a change's page when re-reading its current state failed and the server gave no message of its own. A Retry button follows it.

topic.change.includedInRegion.text: The change this one went live in
topic.change.includedInRegion.description: Accessible name of the box on a change's page that links to the later change it was merged as part of. "This one" is the change being viewed.

topic.change.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the sheet that holds a change's page. A noun: a change to the project that is being built or voted on.

topic.change.bar.titleNumbered.description: Title in the header of a change's page. {{number}} is the change's number. "Change" is a noun: a change to the project that is being built or voted on.

topic.change.bar.title.description: Title in the header of a change's page while the change has no number yet. A noun: a change to the project that is being built.

topic.change.bar.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the header of a change's page: opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the change.

topic.change.bar.openDetails.description: Accessible name of a change's page header title when tapping it opens the Details sheet. {{title}} is the header's title, for example "Change #87". "Details" is the same word the ⋯ menu's Details row uses.

topic.change.bar.openDetailsTitle.description: Tooltip of a change's page header title when tapping it opens the Details sheet, matching the ⋯ menu's Details row.

topic.change.summaryStale.text: Written for an earlier version of this change.
topic.change.summaryStale.description: Note under a change's summary on its page when the change was updated after the summary was written, so the summary may no longer describe it.

topic.change.upstream.from.description: Name of the card on the page of an update: a change given to this version by the project it was made from, the original. {{project}} is the original's name.

topic.change.upstream.made_one.description: Line under "From" on an update's card: how many of the original's changes it brings, {{count}}.

topic.change.upstream.made_other.description: Line under "From" on an update's card: how many of the original's changes it brings, {{count}}.
