topic.change.upstream.in.description: Heading inside the update's card, over what the update does in this version: which of its own changes it keeps, and what it does to its data and connections. {{project}} is this version's name.

topic.change.upstream.keeps_one.description: Line on an update's card: the version's own change, by its title, which the update keeps. {{titles}} is that title.

topic.change.upstream.keeps_other.description: Line on an update's card: the version's own changes, by title, which the update keeps. {{titles}} is the titles, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.keepsMore_one.description: Line on an update's card: the version's own changes, which the update keeps. {{titles}} is the first few titles, already joined into a list, and {{count}} how many more there are.

topic.change.upstream.keepsMore_other.description: Line on an update's card: the version's own changes, which the update keeps. {{titles}} is the first few titles, already joined into a list, and {{count}} how many more there are.

topic.change.upstream.keepsCount_one.description: Line on an update's card when the version has one change of its own, which the update keeps, and its title is not known.

topic.change.upstream.keepsCount_other.description: Line on an update's card: how many of the version's own changes the update keeps, {{count}}, when their titles are not known.

topic.change.upstream.tables_one.text: Adds {{count}} table to your data: {{names}}. None of the data you have changes.
topic.change.upstream.tables_one.description: Line on an update's card: the update makes a new table in the version's database. {{count}} is how many, {{names}} their names, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.tables_other.text: Adds {{count}} tables to your data: {{names}}. None of the data you have changes.
topic.change.upstream.tables_other.description: Line on an update's card: the update makes new tables in the version's database. {{count}} is how many, {{names}} their names, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.dataSame.description: Line on an update's card when the update leaves the version's database as it is.

topic.change.upstream.destructive.description: Line on an update's card when the update removes or reshapes part of the version's database. {{items}} is what it does, as written in the change, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.hosts_one.text: Connects to something new outside Homeroom: {{hosts}}
topic.change.upstream.hosts_one.description: Line on an update's card: the update makes the app talk to a new website or service on the internet. {{hosts}} is its address.

topic.change.upstream.hosts_other.text: Connects to new things outside Homeroom: {{hosts}}
topic.change.upstream.hosts_other.description: Line on an update's card: the update makes the app talk to new websites or services on the internet. {{hosts}} is their addresses, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.hostsNone.description: Line on an update's card when the update makes the app talk to nothing new on the internet.

topic.change.upstream.secrets_one.text: Needs a new key before it goes live: {{keys}}
topic.change.upstream.secrets_one.description: Line on an update's card: the update needs a secret (such as an API key) this version does not have yet. {{keys}} is its name.

topic.change.upstream.secrets_other.text: Needs new keys before it goes live: {{keys}}
topic.change.upstream.secrets_other.description: Line on an update's card: the update needs secrets (such as API keys) this version does not have yet. {{keys}} is their names, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.ai.description: Line on an update's card: with this update the app begins to use an AI model.

topic.change.upstream.storage.description: Line on an update's card: with this update the app begins to keep files, such as uploaded pictures.

topic.change.upstream.skip.title.description: Title of the row under an update's Votes and Testing cards, offering to turn the update down for good.

topic.change.upstream.skip.sub.text: Skip it, and these changes from {{project}} won’t come again. Its later updates still will.
topic.change.upstream.skip.sub.description: Line under "Not for your version?" on an update's page. {{project}} is the name of the project the version was made from.

topic.change.upstream.skip.button.description: Button on an update's page: turns the update down and closes it, leaving the version as it is.

topic.change.upstream.skip.confirmTitle.description: Title of the question asked before an update is skipped. {{project}} is the name of the project the version was made from.

topic.change.upstream.skip.confirmMessag.text: This change closes, and your version stays as it is.
topic.change.upstream.skip.confirmMessag.description: Line of the question asked before an update is skipped.

topic.change.upstream.skip.confirm.description: The confirming button of the question asked before an update is skipped.

topic.change.upstream.skip.failed.text: Could not skip it. Try again.
topic.change.upstream.skip.failed.description: Error on an update's page when "Skip this update" failed and the server gave no reason.

topic.change.upstream.fit.title.text: It clashes with your own changes
topic.change.upstream.fit.title.description: Title of the row under an update's Votes and Testing cards when the original's change and the version's own changes touch the same files.

topic.change.upstream.fit.sub_one.text: {{count}} file needs fitting to your version: {{files}}
topic.change.upstream.fit.sub_one.description: Line under "It clashes with your own changes". {{count}} is how many files, {{files}} their names, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.fit.sub_other.text: {{count}} files need fitting to your version: {{files}}
topic.change.upstream.fit.sub_other.description: Line under "It clashes with your own changes". {{count}} is how many files, {{files}} their names, already joined into a list.

topic.change.upstream.fit.asked.text: Homeroom bot is on it. <0>See the request</0>
topic.change.upstream.fit.asked.description: Shown on an update's page once Homeroom bot was asked to fit it. The tagged words link to the request it builds. "See" is a verb.

topic.change.upstream.fit.failed.text: Could not ask Homeroom bot. Try again.
topic.change.upstream.fit.failed.description: Error on an update's page when "Ask Homeroom bot to fit it" failed and the server gave no reason.

topic.change.codeMissing.text: This proposal’s code didn’t come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub. Its creator can submit it again, or Homeroom restores it when GitHub’s copy of the code arrives.
topic.change.codeMissing.description: Amber notice on a change's page, above its Votes and Testing cards, when the change's code (its branch) is not on Homeroom's own code host because it did not come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub. GitHub is a product name; Homeroom is the product's own name. "GitHub's copy of the code" is the export of the old repositories that GitHub is sending to Homeroom. "Submit it again" means put the same change up again.

topic.change.waitsFor.text: Waits for <0>#{{number}}: {{title}}</0>. This change is built on that change’s branch, so it can go live only after #{{number}} does. Homeroom then moves it onto main and brings it up to date; its checks run again on the result.
topic.change.waitsFor.description: Notice on a change's page, above its Votes and Testing cards, when the change is stacked on another open change: its pull request targets that change's branch instead of main. {{number}} and {{title}} are the other change's number and title; <0></0> links to that change's page. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Homeroom is the product's own name.

topic.change.waitsForUntitled.text: Waits for <0>#{{number}}</0>. This change is built on that change’s branch, so it can go live only after #{{number}} does. Homeroom then moves it onto main and brings it up to date; its checks run again on the result.
topic.change.waitsForUntitled.description: Notice on a change's page, above its Votes and Testing cards, when the change is stacked on another open change that has no title: its pull request targets that change's branch instead of main. {{number}} is the other change's number; <0></0> links to that change's page. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Homeroom is the product's own name.

topic.change.waitsForUnnumbered.text: Waits for <0>another change</0>. This change is built on that change’s branch, so it can go live only after that change does. Homeroom then moves it onto main and brings it up to date; its checks run again on the result.
topic.change.waitsForUnnumbered.description: Notice on a change's page, above its Votes and Testing cards, when the change is stacked on another open change that has no number yet: its pull request targets that change's branch instead of main. <0></0> links to that change's page. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Homeroom is the product's own name.

topic.change.baseNotMain.text: Its pull request targets {{branch}}, not main, and no open change here is built on that branch. Change its base to main on GitHub before it can go live.
topic.change.baseNotMain.description: Amber notice on a change's page, above its Votes and Testing cards, when its pull request targets a branch other than main that no open change in the project uses. {{branch}} is that branch's name as written on GitHub and stays as it is. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. GitHub is a product name.

topic.change.gate.noteSeeFailed.description: The line under the Testing card on a change's page when its checks failed. {{note}} is one or more whole sentences, already worded, saying what happened. <0></0> is a link-style button that opens the Details sheet at the failed checks.

topic.change.gate.seeFailed.description: Link-style button under the Testing card on a change's page when its checks failed and there is nothing else to say: opens the Details sheet at the failed checks.

topic.change.gate.openPage.description: Link-style button after the sentence on the Testing card of a change's page when a failed check opened a page on the change's preview: opens that page on the preview so anyone can see what the check saw.

topic.change.gate.fix.description: Main button on the Testing card of a change's page when its automated checks failed, shown to the change's author: asks the AI agent that built the change to fix what failed. "It" is what failed.

topic.change.gate.fixAsking.description: Text of the Fix it button on the Testing card of a change's page while the request to the AI agent is being sent.

topic.change.gate.fixNote.text: Fix it asks the agent that built this change to fix what failed, using your credits. You can stay on this page: the checks run again by themselves when it’s done.
topic.change.gate.fixNote.description: Line under the Fix it button on the Testing card of a change's page, shown to the change's author. "The agent" is the AI coding agent; credits are what an agent's work is paid with. "It" in the last sentence is the agent.

topic.change.gate.fixing.description: Status at the right of the Testing card's name on a change's page while the AI agent is fixing the checks that failed.

topic.change.gate.fixingLabel.text: The agent is fixing what failed
topic.change.gate.fixingLabel.description: Accessible name of the Testing card's progress bar on a change's page while the AI agent is fixing the checks that failed.

topic.change.gate.fixingNote.text: The agent is fixing what failed. When it’s done, the checks run again by themselves.
topic.change.gate.fixingNote.description: Line under the Testing card of a change's page while the AI agent is fixing the checks that failed. "It" is the agent.

topic.change.gate.noteWatch.description: The line under the Testing card on a change's page while the AI agent fixes the checks that failed. {{note}} is one or more whole sentences, already worded. <0></0> is a link-style button that opens the conversation where the agent is working.

topic.change.gate.closesHead_one.description: Heading of the list under the vote count on a change's Votes card, when the change will close one request if it merges. {{count}} is that number, 1. It is the change.

topic.change.gate.closesHead_other.description: Heading of the list under the vote count on a change's Votes card, when the change will close several requests if it merges. {{count}} is that number. It is the change.

topic.change.gate.closesLine.description: One request a change will close, on its Votes card. <0></0> is the request's number as a link to its page, {{number}} that number, {{title}} the request's title, and {{by}} the name of the person who filed it.

topic.change.gate.closesLineNoFiler.description: One request a change will close, on its Votes card, when nobody knows who filed it. <0></0> is the request's number as a link to its page, {{number}} that number, and {{title}} the request's title.

topic.change.gate.closesLineUntitled.description: A number a change says it would close, on its Votes card, when no request in this project has that number. <0></0> is the number as a link, and {{number}} that number.

topic.change.gate.closesUnconfirmed.description: End of a line naming a request a change will close, on its Votes card, when the person who filed that request has not agreed to it: the change was neither built for that request nor made by that person.

topic.change.gate.closesMore_one.description: Button under the list of requests a change will close, on its Votes card, when one more is hidden. Tapping it shows the hidden line in the same list.

topic.change.gate.closesMore_other.description: Button under the list of requests a change will close, on its Votes card, when some more are hidden. Tapping it shows the hidden lines in the same list.

topic.change.shots.title.description: Name, and accessible name, of the card on a change's page that holds screenshots of the app before and after the change, or the line saying where they are.

topic.change.stream.replies_one.description: Line under a change, over the replies to it, on the change's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.change.stream.replies_other.description: Line under a change, over the replies to it, on the change's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.thread.label.description: Small-caps label over a list on a request's or a change's page: the thread a request's or a change's page is in: every request, change and vote about one piece of work, listed under the page's own post.

topic.thread.item.request.description: What one row of the list is, in its grey line: a request (something people asked a project for). {{number}} is its number. The list is the thread a request's or a change's page is in: every request, change and vote about one piece of work, listed under the page's own post.

topic.thread.item.change.description: What one row of the list is, in its grey line: a change (a proposed edit to the project that people vote on). {{number}} is its number. The list is the thread a request's or a change's page is in: every request, change and vote about one piece of work, listed under the page's own post.

topic.thread.item.changeUnnumbered.description: What one row of the list is, in its grey line, for a change that has no number yet. A change is a proposed edit to the project that people vote on.

change.reload.description: Button beside a live change's status pill when the page open in this tab runs a version of Homeroom from before the change. Pressing it reloads the page onto the running version.

topic.thread.item.close.description: What one row of the list is, in its grey line: a vote on closing the request without building it.

topic.thread.item.decision.description: What one row of the list is, in its grey line: a decision the project's people vote on, such as renaming it.

topic.thread.state.open.description: Where a request in the list stands: nobody has closed it.

topic.thread.state.closed.description: Where a request in the list stands: it was closed.

topic.thread.state.underway.description: Where a change in the list stands: someone is still building it.

topic.thread.state.ready.description: Where a change in the list stands: it has finished building and its checks pass, and it waits for its author to put it up for a vote.

topic.thread.state.voting.description: Where a change, a vote to close or a decision in the list stands: people are voting on it now.

topic.thread.state.live.description: Where a change in the list stands: it was voted in and is running in production now.

topic.thread.state.goingLive.description: Where a change in the list stands: it merged and is on its way to production, not running yet.

topic.thread.state.settled.description: Where a vote to close or a decision in the list stands: the vote is over.

topic.thread.replies_one.description: How many replies people wrote on one item in the list. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.thread.replies_other.description: How many replies people wrote on one item in the list. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.thread.follow.notifyMe.description: Button beside the list on a request's or a change's page, for someone who is not following the thread: get a notification whenever someone replies on anything in it.

topic.thread.follow.notifyMeHint.text: Get a notification when someone replies on anything in this thread.
topic.thread.follow.notifyMeHint.description: Hover text of the Notify me button on a request's or a change's page.

topic.thread.follow.mute.description: The same button for someone who is following the thread (they asked, built, voted or posted there, or pressed Notify me): stop its replies notifying them.

topic.thread.follow.muteHint.text: Replies here notify you. Press to stop them.
topic.thread.follow.muteHint.description: Hover text of the Mute button on a request's or a change's page.

topic.thread.follow.muted.description: The same button once the thread is muted: its replies do not notify the person. Pressing it again unmutes the thread.

topic.thread.follow.mutedHint.text: Muted: replies here do not notify you, until you reply yourself. Press to unmute.
topic.thread.follow.mutedHint.description: Hover text of the button on a request's or a change's page while the thread is muted.

topic.thread.follow.unmute.description: A row of a request's or a change's ⋯ menu, once the person has muted its thread: notifications for replies in the thread start again. A verb in the imperative.

topic.thread.move.merge.description: Line under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page: someone proposed merging this thread into another one. {{number}} is the other thread's number.

topic.thread.move.split.description: Line under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page: someone proposed moving items out of this thread into a thread of their own. {{what}} lists them, for example "#9".

topic.thread.move.breakup_one.text: Proposed: break #{{number}} up into {{count}} smaller request
topic.thread.move.breakup_one.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. A waiting break-up of the request into smaller requests in the same thread. {{number}} is the request, {{count}} how many parts.

topic.thread.move.breakup_other.text: Proposed: break #{{number}} up into {{count}} smaller requests
topic.thread.move.breakup_other.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. A waiting break-up of the request into smaller requests in the same thread. {{number}} is the request, {{count}} how many parts.

topic.thread.move.breakUp.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Button: opens the form that breaks this request into smaller requests in the same thread.

topic.thread.move.breakUpAbout.text: Each part becomes a request of its own here, with its own change and vote. #{{number}} closes with the last of them.
topic.thread.move.breakUpAbout.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Over the break-up form. {{number}} is the request being broken up.

topic.thread.move.partTitle_one.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Field in the break-up form: a smaller request's title. {{count}} is which part it is.

topic.thread.move.partTitle_other.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Field in the break-up form: a smaller request's title. {{count}} is which part it is.

topic.thread.move.partDone.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Field in the break-up form: what that smaller request is done when. Optional.

topic.thread.move.addPart.description: On a request's page, the thread's moves (merge, split, break up), decided by its requesters agreeing or 24 hours with no objection. Button in the break-up form: one more smaller request.

topic.thread.move.pending_one.text: Happens in {{count}} hour unless someone objects
topic.thread.move.pending_one.description: Second half of the line under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page about a proposed merge or split: when it happens on its own. {{count}} is the hours left.

topic.thread.move.pending_other.text: Happens in {{count}} hours unless someone objects
topic.thread.move.pending_other.description: Second half of the line under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page about a proposed merge or split: when it happens on its own. {{count}} is the hours left.

topic.thread.move.voting.text: Up for a vote, as someone objected
topic.thread.move.voting.description: Second half of the line under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page about a proposed merge or split once someone objected: the project's people vote on it.

topic.thread.move.agree.description: Button beside a proposed merge or split of a thread: the person, who asked for something in it, agrees. Once everyone who asked agrees, it happens.

topic.thread.move.object.description: Button beside a proposed merge or split of a thread: the person objects, which puts it to the project's vote.

topic.thread.move.consentAsk.text: Move into #{{number}}'s thread? Change #{{change}} closes this request, and lives there.
topic.thread.move.consentAsk.description: On a request's page, a change for several requests asks its other requester whether this request's thread should join the change's. {{number}} is the number of the thread the change lives in, {{change}} the change's number.

topic.thread.move.consentYes.description: Button beside a change's question on a request's page: the requester agrees to move this request's thread into the change's.

topic.thread.move.consentSeparate.description: Button beside a change's question on a request's page: the requester keeps this request's thread where it is. The change still closes the request.

topic.thread.move.consentWaiting.description: On a request's page, under a change's question about moving this request's thread into the change's, shown to everyone who cannot answer it: {{names}} are the requesters who still have to answer, by username.

topic.thread.move.mergeInto.description: Button under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page: propose merging this thread into another one about the same work.

topic.thread.move.splitOut.description: Button under the list of a thread (every request, change and vote about one piece of work) on a request's or a change's page: propose moving one item out of this thread into a thread of its own.

topic.thread.move.number.description: Box in the form for merging a thread: the number of the request or change whose thread this one goes into.

topic.thread.move.choose.description: First, empty choice of the picker in the form for splitting an item out of a thread.

topic.thread.move.propose.description: Send button of the form for merging or splitting a thread.

topic.thread.move.failed.description: Error under the merge / split controls of a thread when the request failed.

topic.change.stream.noReplies.description: Line under a change, on its page, when nobody has replied to it.

topic.change.stream.conversationOn.description: Line under a change, on its page, when the change was built for a request and has no replies of its own: the conversation about the change is on that request's page instead. <0> is the link to the request, shown as its number; {{number}} is that number. Nothing follows the link on the line.

topic.change.stream.moreConversationOn.text: More of the conversation is on <0>#{{number}}</0>
topic.change.stream.moreConversationOn.description: Line above the "N replies" row on a change's page, when the change was built for a request and also has replies of its own: the fuller conversation is on that request's page. <0> is the link to the request, shown as its number; {{number}} is that number.

topic.change.stream.loading.description: Line under a change, on its page, while the replies to it are being fetched.

topic.change.stream.loadEarlier.description: Button at the top of the replies on a change's page: fetches the older replies before the ones shown. Load is a verb.

topic.change.stream.tryIt.description: Link-style button at the end of the line "The preview is ready" among the replies on a change's page: opens the preview so the person can use the change before voting. "It" is the change.

topic.change.line.postedSpec.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description the change is built from) was posted. {{author}} is who posted it, a username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.change.line.postedSpecUnnamed.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description the change is built from) was posted. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{version}} is the plan's version number.

topic.change.line.botPlan.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: Homeroom bot's plan (the written description the change is built from). {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version. {{title}} is the plan's title. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.change.line.previewReady.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: the preview build of the change finished and can be opened. A "Try it" button follows it. No full stop.

topic.change.line.askedForApproval.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: the change was put up for the members' vote. {{author}} is the username of who did it, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.unnamedAskedForApprova.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: the change was put up for the members' vote, when it is not known by whom. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.votedYes.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour of the change. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedYesReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour of the change and gave a reason. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote, in their own words; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedYesEarlier.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted yes on an earlier version
topic.change.line.votedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedYesEarlierReason.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted yes on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.votedYesEarlierReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour and gave a reason, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedNo.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against the change. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedNoReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against the change and gave a reason. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote, in their own words; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedNoEarlier.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted no on an earlier version
topic.change.line.votedNoEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedNoEarlierReason.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted no on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.votedNoEarlierReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against and gave a reason, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYes.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour of the change, when it is not known who. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour of the change and gave a reason, when it is not known who. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.text: Voted yes on an earlier version
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.text: Voted yes on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour and gave a reason, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNo.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against the change, when it is not known who. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against the change and gave a reason, when it is not known who. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlier.text: Voted no on an earlier version
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlierR.text: Voted no on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlierR.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against and gave a reason, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.requests.region.description: Accessible name of the row on a change's page, under its summary, that names the requests (filed issues) the change is meant to resolve.

topic.requests.addresses.description: Label at the start of the row on a change's page that names the requests (filed issues) the change was built for: the first request follows it as a chip, with a "+N more" button when there are others.

topic.requests.more_one.description: Button after the first request on the "Addresses" row of a change's page, when the change resolves more than one request: shows the others, one to a line. {{count}} is how many others there are. Keep the plus sign.

topic.requests.more_other.description: Button after the first request on the "Addresses" row of a change's page, when the change resolves more than one request: shows the others, one to a line. {{count}} is how many others there are. Keep the plus sign.

topic.requests.showLess.description: Replaces the "+N more" button on the "Addresses" row of a change's page while the other requests are shown: hides them again.

topic.requests.selectedCount_one.description: Small heading over the requests currently linked, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{count}} is how many are selected.

topic.requests.selectedCount_other.description: Small heading over the requests currently linked, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{count}} is how many are selected.

topic.requests.remaining_one.description: Shown opposite "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests: how many more requests may still be linked before the limit. {{count}} is that number.

topic.requests.remaining_other.description: Shown opposite "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests: how many more requests may still be linked before the limit. {{count}} is that number.

topic.requests.remove.description: Accessible name of the X button on one selected request in the editor of a change's linked requests: unlinks it. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.noneSelected.description: Shown under "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests when none is selected.

topic.requests.addAnother.description: Label of the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests: finds an existing request (filed issue) to link.

topic.requests.searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests. A request can be found by its number or by words in its title.

topic.requests.matches.description: Accessible name of the list of search results under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests.

topic.requests.addNamed.description: Accessible name of one search result in the editor of a change's linked requests: selecting it links that request. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.addNumbered.description: Accessible name of the search result that links a request by the exact number the person typed, when its title is not known. {{number}} is that number. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.addByNumber.description: Text of the search result that links a request by the exact number the person typed, shown where a request's title would be. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.untitled.description: Stand-in title for a selected request whose real title is not known, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{number}} is the request's number. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.noMatches.text: No matching open requests. Enter a request number to add it.
topic.requests.noMatches.description: Shown under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests when nothing matches what was typed.

topic.requests.searchHelp.text: Searches open requests in this project. You can always add one by its number.
topic.requests.searchHelp.description: Help line under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests. Open requests are the ones not yet closed.

topic.requests.numberTooLarge.text: “{{input}}” is too large to be an issue number.
topic.requests.numberTooLarge.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the number typed is too big to be a request's number. {{input}} is exactly what the person typed. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.chooseOrEnter.text: Choose a matching issue or enter its issue number.
topic.requests.chooseOrEnter.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when Enter is pressed and the text typed matches no request and is not a number. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.tooMany_one.text: A change can link at most {{count}} requests.
topic.requests.tooMany_one.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the limit is reached. {{count}} is the largest number of requests one change may be linked to.

topic.requests.tooMany_other.text: A change can link at most {{count}} requests.
topic.requests.tooMany_other.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the limit is reached. {{count}} is the largest number of requests one change may be linked to.

topic.requests.updateFailed.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when saving was refused and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.requests.networkError.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the save request could not reach the server.

topic.requests.saved.description: Confirmation under the "Addresses" line of a change after its linked requests were saved. "Issues" is another word for requests here.

topic.requests.savedSyncPending.text: Issues saved. The pull request could not be updated yet; saving again will retry it.
topic.requests.savedSyncPending.description: Confirmation under the "Addresses" line of a change after its linked requests were saved in Homeroom but could not be written to the change's pull request on GitHub. "Issues" is another word for requests here.

topic.requests.save.description: Main button of the editor of a change's linked requests: saves which requests the change is linked to. "Requests" is a noun here.

topic.requests.saving.description: Text of the main button in the editor of a change's linked requests while the links are being saved.

topic.request.addressedByRegion.description: Accessible name of the box on a request's page that links to the change being built or voted on to resolve it. "Issue" is another word for the request.

topic.request.closedBand.closed.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when neither the date nor the way it was closed is known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request, not the verb for closing a window. <0></0> draws it bold.

topic.request.closedBand.when.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when only the date is known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

topic.request.closedBand.whenByChange.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when a merged change closed it: closed, on this date, by this change. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> and <3></3> are separator dots hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date; <4></4> holds the word that introduces the change; <5></5> is a link showing the change's number and title, which fills itself in: leave it empty and put it where the change's name belongs.

topic.request.closedBand.byChange.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when a merged change closed it and the date is not known: closed by this change. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the word that introduces the change; <3></3> is a link showing the change's number and title, which fills itself in: leave it empty and put it where the change's name belongs.

topic.request.closedBand.byChangeLabel.description: Accessible name of the link, in the band at the top of a closed request, to the change that closed it. {{change}} is the change's reference, for example #10, and {{title}} its title.

topic.request.body.title.description: Heading over the description of a request (a filed issue) on its page.

topic.request.body.editTitle.text: Edit this request (you asked for it)
topic.request.body.editTitle.description: Hover text of the pencil button beside "About this request", shown only to the person who filed the request. "You asked for it" means: you are the one who made this request.

topic.request.body.editLabel.description: Accessible name of the pencil button beside "About this request": lets the person who filed the request rewrite its description. A verb phrase.

topic.request.body.empty.description: Shown to the person who filed a request, on its page, when the request has no description.

topic.request.body.unavailable.text: This request is not available right now.
topic.request.body.unavailable.description: Error under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page and in its About sheet, when the edit cannot be saved because the request's project is not loaded.

topic.request.body.saveFailed.description: Error under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page and in its About sheet, when saving failed and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.request.body.save.description: Main button under the description editor of a request: saves the edited description. "Body" is the main text of the request.

topic.request.body.saving.description: Text of the main button under the description editor of a request while the description is being saved.

topic.request.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the sheet that holds a request's page. A noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed in the project.

topic.request.bar.title.description: Title in the header of a request's page. {{number}} is the request's number. "Request" is a noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed.

topic.request.bar.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the header of a request's page: opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the request.

topic.request.bar.kickerDone.description: Small line above the title in the header of a request's page, once the request has been built and voted in. {{number}} is the request's number. "Request" is a noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed.

topic.request.bar.kickerClosed.description: Small line above the title in the header of a request's page, once the request was closed without anything being built for it. {{number}} is the request's number. "Request" is a noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed.

topic.request.words.showMore.description: Button under a request's own words on its page, and under a change's summary on a change's page, while the text is folded after four lines: unfolds all of it.

topic.request.words.showLess.description: Button under a request's own words on its page, and under a change's summary on a change's page, once the text is unfolded: folds it back to four lines.

topic.request.words.translate.description: Button beside Show more under someone else's request on its page: shows its title and words in the language the reader uses Homeroom in. A verb.

topic.request.editor.label.description: Accessible name of the text box in which the person who filed a request rewrites its words, on the request's page. A noun.

topic.request.editor.saving.description: Replaces "Save" on the button under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page, while the edit is being saved.

topic.request.status.label.description: Accessible name of the card on a request's page that shows how far the request has come: asked, plan written, built, voted in.

topic.request.ownAgent.summary.text: Build it with your own Claude Code
topic.request.ownAgent.summary.description: Folded line under the status card on a request's page; opening it shows a link that hands this request to Claude Code on the web, on the person's own Claude plan. "Claude Code" is a product name.

topic.request.agentSession.summary.text: Build it in an agent session
topic.request.agentSession.summary.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's page, next to "Build it with your own Claude Code": starts a session where the viewer builds the request with an AI coding agent. An agent session is a working conversation with an AI coding agent. "Build" is a verb.

topic.workWithBot.ask.description: Quiet button under a change on a request's page and on a change's own page, when the change is not up for a vote: opens a thread only the viewer can see, in their chat with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant), to ask about this change. "Privately" says the thread is theirs alone.

topic.workWithBot.askTitle.text: Ask Homeroom bot about this change in a thread only you can see
topic.workWithBot.askTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Ask Homeroom bot privately" button under a change. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

topic.workWithBot.suggest.description: Quiet button under a change that is up for a vote, on a request's page and on a change's own page: opens a thread only the viewer can see, in their chat with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant), to sketch a revision of this change. "Privately" says the thread is theirs alone.

topic.workWithBot.suggestTitle.text: Sketch a revision of this change with Homeroom bot, in a thread only you can see
topic.workWithBot.suggestTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Suggest a change privately" button under a change that is up for a vote. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

topic.workWithBot.opening.description: The "Ask Homeroom bot privately" and "Suggest a change privately" buttons' words while their private thread with Homeroom bot opens.

topic.workWithBot.failed.text: The thread with Homeroom bot could not be started just now. Try again in a minute.
topic.workWithBot.failed.description: Toast when "Ask Homeroom bot privately" or "Suggest a change privately" could not open its private thread with Homeroom bot, the platform's assistant.

topic.request.ownAgent.lead.text: Claude Code opens with a prompt to build this request already typed. Check it and press send. It runs on your own Claude plan.
topic.request.ownAgent.lead.description: Explains, on a request's page, what the "Open in Claude Code" link below it does.

topic.request.ownAgent.open.description: Link on a request's page that opens Claude Code on the web in a new tab with a prompt to build this request already typed. "Claude Code" is a product name.

topic.request.ownAgent.needsHeading.description: Heading over the short list, on a request's page, of what the person needs for the "Open in Claude Code" link to work.

topic.request.ownAgent.needs.plan.text: A Claude Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan with Claude Code on the web
topic.request.ownAgent.needs.plan.description: First item of the "You need" list under the "Open in Claude Code" link on a request's page. Plan names are product names.

topic.request.ownAgent.needs.github.description: Second item of the "You need" list under the "Open in Claude Code" link on a request's page: the person has connected their GitHub account in Claude Code on the web.

topic.request.ownAgent.needs.connector.description: Third item of the "You need" list under the "Open in Claude Code" link on a request's page: the Homeroom connector is added to the person's Claude account. Followed by a tick when done, or an "Add it" link.

topic.request.ownAgent.needs.connectorAd.description: Link after "Homeroom connected in Claude" on a request's page, when Homeroom cannot see the connector yet: opens the connector settings that show how to add it.

topic.request.ownAgent.needs.done.description: Screen-reader text after a "You need" item on a request's page that is already set up, read in place of the tick.

topic.request.status.specVersionReady.text: Plan v{{version}} is ready for comments.
topic.request.status.specVersionReady.description: Sentence in the status card on a request's page once a plan (the written description of the change that would answer the request) has been posted. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.status.specReady.text: A plan is ready for comments.
topic.request.status.specReady.description: Sentence in the status card on a request's page once a plan (the written description of the change that would answer the request) has been posted and its version is not known.

topic.request.stage.asked.description: First of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): somebody asked for this. A past participle describing the request.

topic.request.stage.spec.description: Second of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): a plan, the written description of the change that would answer the request, has been posted. A noun.

topic.request.stage.built.description: Third of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): a change that answers the request has been built. A past participle describing the request.

topic.request.stage.voted.description: Last of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): the change that answers the request was approved by the members' vote and went live.

topic.request.botPlan.subYours.description: On a request's page, under the title of Homeroom bot's plan for it: the plan waits for the reader, who asked for it, to press Build it. {{number}} is the request's number.

topic.request.botPlan.subTheirs.text: @{{requester}}'s plan for #{{number}} · any member can build it
topic.request.botPlan.subTheirs.description: On a request's page, under the title of Homeroom bot's plan for it, for anyone but the person who asked for it: whose request it is, and that any member of the community may press Build it. {{requester}} is that person's username; {{number}} is the request's number.

topic.request.botPlan.subAnyone.text: Plan for #{{number}} · any member can build it
topic.request.botPlan.subAnyone.description: On a request's page, under the title of Homeroom bot's plan for it, when the person who asked for it is not known: any member of the community may press Build it. {{number}} is the request's number.

topic.request.botPlan.subBuilding.description: On a request's page, under the title of Homeroom bot's plan for it once somebody pressed Build it: the bot is building what the plan describes. It replaces the line that said the plan waits for Build it. {{number}} is the request's number.

topic.request.botPlan.readWhole.description: On a request's page, a row under the lines of Homeroom bot's plan: opens the whole written plan.

topic.request.botPlan.readWholeLength.text: Read the whole plan <1>· about {{chars}} characters</1>
topic.request.botPlan.readWholeLength.description: On a request's page, the row under the lines of Homeroom bot's plan: opens the whole written plan, and says how long it is. {{chars}} is a rounded number of characters, already formatted (for example 20,000). The middle dot stands between the two parts.

topic.request.botPlan.quote.description: On a request's page, the words a reply quoting Homeroom bot's plan shows when the plan has no title (Change something stages that quote in the reply box).

topic.request.botPlan.refused.changing.text: Somebody asked for a change to this plan, and the next plan is on its way. Build it comes back with it.
topic.request.botPlan.refused.changing.description: On a request's page, under Homeroom bot's plan, after Build it was pressed: it did not build, because a change to the plan was asked for and a newer plan is being written.

topic.request.botPlan.refused.allowance.text: Your building time for this week is used up, so this plan was not built. It resets on Monday.
topic.request.botPlan.refused.allowance.description: On a request's page, under Homeroom bot's plan, after Build it was pressed: it did not build, because the presser's weekly allowance of Homeroom bot's building time is spent. The allowance resets each Monday.

topic.request.botPlan.refused.gone.text: This plan is no longer waiting: it was built, replaced or stopped.
topic.request.botPlan.refused.gone.description: On a request's page, under Homeroom bot's plan, after Build it was pressed: the plan had already been built, replaced by a newer one, or stopped, so nothing was built.

topic.request.botPlan.refused.other.text: Build it did not go through. Try again in a moment.
topic.request.botPlan.refused.other.description: On a request's page, under Homeroom bot's plan, after Build it was pressed: the request failed for another reason, such as the connection.

topic.request.spec.kicker.description: Small upper-case label over the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the plan has no version number. A noun: the written description the change is built from.

topic.request.spec.kickerVersion.description: Small upper-case label over the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan). "Plan" is a noun: the written description the change is built from. {{version}} is its version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.spec.kickerReplaced.description: Small heading over a plan's card on a request's page, for a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed that a newer plan replaced. {{version}} is the plan's version number. "Replaced" is an adjective: a newer plan took its place.

topic.request.spec.kickerStopped.description: Small heading over a plan's card on a request's page, for a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed that no longer waits for the person who asked for it to say Build it. {{version}} is the plan's version number.

topic.request.spec.by.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. {{author}} is a username, or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot.

topic.request.spec.bySystem.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place.

topic.request.spec.bySomeone.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it.

topic.request.spec.byAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. {{author}} is a username, or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot. {{time}} is when, already formatted, for example 2:41 PM or Oct 5; keep it inside <0></0>.

topic.request.spec.bySystemAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place. {{time}} is when, already worded.

topic.request.spec.bySomeoneAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{time}} is when, already formatted.

topic.request.spec.read.description: Button on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): opens the plan to read beside the page. A verb in the imperative, not the past tense.

topic.request.spec.readNamed.description: Accessible name of the Read button on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan). {{title}} is the plan's title. Read is a verb in the imperative.

topic.thread.page.fromPlan.description: On a request's page, under a change built from a plan posted on the request: says which plan it carries out, beside the plan's Read button. {{title}} is the plan's title.

topic.thread.page.fromPlanVersion.text: Built from v{{version}} of the plan "{{title}}"
topic.thread.page.fromPlanVersion.description: On a request's page, under a change built from a numbered version of a plan posted on the request: says which version it carries out, beside the plan's Read button. {{version}} is the plan's version number (1, 2, 3) and {{title}} is the plan's title.

topic.thread.page.newerPlan.description: After "Built from v1 of the plan ..." on a change whose plan has a newer version on the request, by the same person: says a newer version exists. {{version}} is that newer version's number (2, 3).

topic.thread.page.newerPlanOther.description: After "Built from v1 of the plan ..." on a change whose plan has a newer version on the request, posted by somebody else: says whose newer plan exists. {{author}} is the person's name, without an @.

topic.request.spec.opening.description: Replaces "Read" on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan) while the plan is being fetched.

topic.request.spec.untitled.description: Stands in for the title of a plan that has none, on its card under a request and at the top of the reader that opens it. The plan is the written description of the change that Homeroom's assistant posted on the request's GitHub issue.

topic.request.stream.replies_one.description: Line under a request, over the replies to it, on the request's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.request.stream.replies_other.description: Line under a request, over the replies to it, on the request's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.request.stream.onChange.description: Small words after the time of a reply or a line in a request's discussion that was written on one of the request's changes, which has no page of its own: the request's page holds the discussion of the whole piece of work. {{number}} is the change's number.

topic.request.stream.onChangeUnnumbered.description: Small words after the time of a reply or a line in a request's discussion that was written on one of the request's changes that has no number yet: the request's page holds the discussion of the whole piece of work.

topic.request.stream.onRequest.description: Small words after the time of a reply in a request's discussion that was written on another request of the same merged thread: {{number}} is that other request's number.

topic.request.stream.noReplies.description: Line under a request, on its page, when nobody has replied to it.

topic.request.stream.loading.description: Line under a request, on its page, while the replies to it are being fetched.

topic.request.stream.loadEarlier.description: Button at the top of the replies on a request's page: fetches the older replies before the ones shown. Load is a verb.

topic.request.stream.earlierOnGitHub.text: Earlier GitHub comments aren’t shown here. <0>Read them on GitHub</0>
topic.request.stream.earlierOnGitHub.description: Line at the top of the replies on a request's page when only the newest comments from the request's GitHub issue were fetched. <0></0> is a link to the issue on GitHub, where the rest can be read. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.earlierNotShown.text: Earlier GitHub comments aren’t shown here.
topic.request.stream.earlierNotShown.description: Line at the top of the replies on a request's page when only the newest comments from the request's GitHub issue were fetched and the issue's address is not known. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.timeOnGitHub.description: Beside the author's name on a reply, on a request's page, that was written as a comment on the request's GitHub issue rather than in Homeroom. {{time}} is when it was written, already formatted; <0></0> holds it and <1></1> holds the note saying where it was written. Keep both tags. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.onGitHub.description: Beside the author's name on a reply, on a request's page, that was written as a comment on the request's GitHub issue rather than in Homeroom, when its time is not known. Lower case: it follows the name. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecVersion.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted. {{author}} is the username of who posted it, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecVersionUn.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{version}} is the plan's version number.

topic.request.stream.postedSpec.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted on the request's GitHub issue. {{author}} is who posted it, a username or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecSystem.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted on the request's GitHub issue. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place. Keep the <0> tag around the word.

topic.request.stream.botPlanBuilding.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. I'm building it now.
topic.request.stream.botPlanBuilding.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot (an assistant that builds requests, speaking in the first person) posted its plan (the written description of the change) and is building it. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version. {{title}} is the plan's title. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanWaiting.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. Nothing is built yet. Waiting for @{{requester}} to say Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanWaiting.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change) and builds nothing until the person who asked for it approves it. It says plainly that nothing has been built yet. {{version}} is the plan's version number; {{title}} is the plan's title; {{requester}} is that person's username, after an @. "Build it" is the name of the button they tap: keep it as the button reads in your language. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanWaitingUnnam.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. Nothing is built yet. Waiting for the person who asked for it to say Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanWaitingUnnam.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change) and builds nothing until the person who asked for the request approves it; used when that person cannot be named. It says plainly that nothing has been built yet. {{version}} is the plan's version number; {{title}} is the plan's title. "Build it" is the name of the button they tap. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanReplaced.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. A newer plan replaced it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanReplaced.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed for the change, which stopped waiting because the bot planned the request again; the newer plan is further down. {{version}} is the plan's version number and {{title}} its title.

topic.request.stream.botPlanStopped.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. It stopped waiting for Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanStopped.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed for the change, which no longer waits for the person who asked for it (nobody said Build it within a week, or the request was settled another way). {{version}} is the plan's version number and {{title}} its title. "Build it" is the name of the button that person taps: keep it as the button reads.

topic.request.stream.botPlan.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change). {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version. {{title}} is the plan's title. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.claimed.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a member took the request on. {{member}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.claimedPlain.description: Plain-text form of the line saying a member took a request on, for places that show a request's events as text only. {{member}} is their username. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.read.description: Link-style button at the end of the line saying a plan was posted, among the replies on a request's page: opens that plan to read. A verb in the imperative, not the past tense.

topic.run.build.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of building a preview of the app with the change. A noun.

topic.run.checks.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the automated checks the app declares, which open its screens and look for what should be there.

topic.run.checks.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progress.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going: {{ran}} checks have run out of {{expected}} declared. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is a question mark when the total is not known.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.starting.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when the checks are about to begin and none has run yet.

topic.run.checks.waitingForSlot.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the run is queued behind other runs. A slot is a free place to run.

topic.run.checks.afterBuild.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the preview is still being built: the checks will start once the build finishes.

topic.run.checks.didNotRun.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when no run is going and no check ran, for example because the build failed.

topic.run.unit.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the project's own automated code tests.

topic.run.unit.cloning.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the project's code is being copied before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.installing.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the code's dependencies are being installed before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.reused_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when this run did not run the unit tests again but reused an earlier pass of the same commit. {{passed}} is how many tests passed then, already formatted ("13,214"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{when}} is how long ago that was (for example "12m ago"), {{run}} the start of that run's id (for example "832c9d27").

topic.run.unit.reused_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when this run did not run the unit tests again but reused an earlier pass of the same commit. {{passed}} is how many tests passed then, already formatted ("13,214"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{when}} is how long ago that was (for example "12m ago"), {{run}} the start of that run's id (for example "832c9d27").

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progress.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running: {{ran}} tests have run out of {{expected}}. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is an estimate from the last run, written with a leading ~ ("~13,214"), or a question mark when not known.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.details.title.description: Heading, and accessible name, of the sheet that opens over a change's page with its technical side: the pull request, the steps to going live with their checks, and the full description.

topic.details.openOnGitHub.description: Link in the Details sheet of a change whose pull request is on GitHub, beside its pull-request number: opens that pull request on GitHub in a new tab. "Open" is a verb; GitHub is a product name.

topic.details.viewCode.description: Link in the Details sheet of a change whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub, beside its number: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

topic.details.description.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the full technical description of the change. A noun.

topic.details.shots.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the technical record of its before-and-after screenshots: what was captured and what was left out. "Screenshot" names one of the pictures.

card.pill.goesLiveIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its approval window counts down: the change will be merged and go live when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.pill.setAsideIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its rejection window counts down: the proposal was voted down and will be closed without merging when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.tally.yes.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped, when nobody voted against it. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted and {{needed}} how many were needed to pass, for example "2/2 yes".

card.tally.yesNo.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped, after the yes votes against the number needed, then the no votes. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, {{needed}} how many were needed to pass and {{no}} how many voted no, for example "3/3 yes · 1 no".

card.tally.passed.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped with at least as many yes votes as it needed and nobody against it. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, for example "3 yes". The number needed is in the hover text.

card.tally.passedNo.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped with at least as many yes votes as it needed, then the no votes. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted and {{no}} how many voted no, for example "3 yes · 1 no". The number needed is in the hover text.

card.tally.title.text: {{yes}} yes and {{no}} no. It needed {{needed}} yes to pass.
card.tally.title.description: Hover text for the final vote count beside the Live status of a change that has shipped: the whole sentence the short count stands for. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, {{no}} how many voted no and {{needed}} how many yes votes were needed to pass.

card.countdown.daysHours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, a day or more, shown inside "Goes live in …". {{days}} and {{hours}} are numbers; d and h abbreviate days and hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.days.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of days. {{days}} is a number; d abbreviates days. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hoursMinutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, between an hour and a day. {{hours}} and {{minutes}} are numbers; h and m abbreviate hours and minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of hours. {{hours}} is a number; h abbreviates hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.minutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when under an hour. {{minutes}} is a number, at least 1; m abbreviates minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.pill.moreReasons_one.text: and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_one.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.moreReasons_other.text: and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_other.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.text: {{count}} advisory vote from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.description: Tooltip on the small +N beside a proposal's vote tally. {{count}} is the number of votes cast by members who are not among the project's approvers; those votes are shown but do not count toward merging the change.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_other.text: {{count}} advisory votes from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
