communityCard.line.approvers.short_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} approvers (there is {{count}}) say yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.short_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvers than the project has. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many there are.

communityCard.line.approvers.short_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} approvers (there are {{count}}) say yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.short_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvers than the project has. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many there are.

communityCard.line.fixed_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} member approves it.
communityCard.line.fixed_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's settings ask for a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is that number.

communityCard.line.fixed_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} members approve it.
communityCard.line.fixed_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's settings ask for a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is that number.

communityCard.line.members.some_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} active members approves it.
communityCard.line.members.some_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's active members must approve. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.members.some_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} active members approve it.
communityCard.line.members.some_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's active members must approve. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.members.short_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} active members (there is {{count}}) approve it.
communityCard.line.members.short_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvals than the project has active members. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.members.short_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} active members (there are {{count}}) approve it.
communityCard.line.members.short_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvals than the project has active members. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.members.all_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} active members approve it.
communityCard.line.members.all_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every active member must approve. {{count}} is how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.members.all_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} active members approve it.
communityCard.line.members.all_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every active member must approve. {{count}} is how many active members there are.

communityCard.line.approvers.only.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and the approver says yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.only.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project has one approver.

communityCard.line.approvers.both.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and both approvers say yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.both.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's two approvers must both say yes.

communityCard.line.members.only.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and the only active member approves it.
communityCard.line.members.only.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project has one active member.

communityCard.line.members.both.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and both active members approve it.
communityCard.line.members.both.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's two active members must both approve.

communityCard.lineShort.you.text: Goes live when its checks pass and you approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.you.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, on a project that is just the viewer's. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.anyOf.text: Goes live when its checks pass and <0></0><1>{{names}}</1> says yes.
communityCard.lineShort.anyOf.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where any one of the named approvers is enough. <0></0> is where their faces go; <1> wraps {{names}}, their account names joined with "or" (for example "evan or snait"), shown bold. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.allOf.text: Goes live when its checks pass and <0></0><1>{{names}}</1> say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.allOf.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every named approver has to say yes. <0></0> is where their faces go; <1> wraps {{names}}, their account names joined with "and" (for example "evan and snait"), shown bold. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.some_o.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers says yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.some_o.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many approvers there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.some_o.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.some_o.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many approvers there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.all_on.text: Goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} approvers say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.all_on.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every one of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many approvers there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.all_ot.text: Goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} approvers say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.all_ot.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every one of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many approvers there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.short_.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} approvers (there is {{count}}) say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.short_.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvers than the project has. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.short_.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} approvers (there are {{count}}) say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.short_.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvers than the project has. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.fixed_one.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} member approves it.
communityCard.lineShort.fixed_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's settings ask for a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is that number. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.fixed_other.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} members approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.fixed_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's settings ask for a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is that number. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.some_one.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} active members approves it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.some_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's active members must approve. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.some_oth.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} active members approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.some_oth.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's active members must approve. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.short_on.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} active members (there is {{count}}) approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.short_on.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvals than the project has active members. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.short_ot.text: Goes live when its checks pass and {{required}} active members (there are {{count}}) approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.short_ot.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the rule asks for more approvals than the project has active members. {{required}} is how many it asks for, {{count}} how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.all_one.text: Goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} active members approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.all_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every active member must approve. {{count}} is how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.all_othe.text: Goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} active members approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.all_othe.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every active member must approve. {{count}} is how many active members there are. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.only.text: Goes live when its checks pass and the approver says yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.only.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project has one approver. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.approvers.both.text: Goes live when its checks pass and both approvers say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.approvers.both.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's two approvers must both say yes. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.only.text: Goes live when its checks pass and the only active member approves it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.only.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project has one active member. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.lineShort.members.both.text: Goes live when its checks pass and both active members approve it.
communityCard.lineShort.members.both.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where the project's two active members must both approve. The shorter wording drawn where the card is narrow, as on a phone; it leaves out "A change".

communityCard.rule.rules.description: Button at the end of the approval rule's line on the Workshop tab of a project's page, for people who may change the rule: opens the Members & approvals dialog at its approvals section, where a change to the rule is proposed and voted on.

page.title.hub.description: Title of a project's Hub page, the first of its places: who is here and who it is for, its actions, its trend and what needs the person. A noun, the name of the place.

places.tray.name.description: Accessible name of the tray that slides in from the left on a phone and lists a project's places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and its channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

allItems.themes.topics.description: Small upper-case heading over a project's topics on the By category view of its All items page. Topics are the categories its members set up, each with a chat channel of its own. A noun.

allItems.themes.other.description: Small upper-case heading on the By category view of a project's All items page, over the categories that are not one of its topics (the ones the members set up, listed above it).

allItems.theme.discuss.description: Link at the foot of a topic's card on the By category view of a project's All items page: opens that topic's chat channel. {{channel}} is the channel's handle, written after its #, for example onboarding. Keep the # before it and the arrow at the end.

topic.change.gate.release.description: The last sentence of the line under the Votes card on the page of a change to Homeroom itself that has merged. {{release}} is a finished sentence saying when the change goes live, for example "Merged; goes live in the next release (about 8 minutes)"; this entry adds only the full stop that ends it.

diagram.kind.rename.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram shows a rename: an old name, an arrow, the new name.

diagram.kind.flow.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram shows the steps of something before the change and after it. Keep the arrow.

diagram.kind.changes.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram lists what the change adds, changes and removes.

diagram.kind.numbers.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram compares figures before and after the change, with bars.

diagram.kind.mermaid.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram is a free-form picture its author drew.

diagram.label.description: Accessible name a screen reader reads for a change's diagram. {{kind}} is the diagram's label, for example "Rename" or "What changes"; {{text}} is the diagram said in words, one or more whole sentences.

diagram.source.decision.description: Small line under a diagram on a Needs-you card: the picture was drawn from the facts of a group decision (a rename, a closed request, a secret setting), not by a person.

diagram.source.files.description: Small line under a picture on a Needs-you card: the picture (which parts of the project the change touches) was made from the files the change edits.

diagram.source.author.description: Small line under a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page): the person or agent who made the change supplied this diagram.

diagram.source.authorMermaid.text: Diagram by the change’s author · Mermaid
diagram.source.authorMermaid.description: Small line under a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page): the change's author supplied it, written in Mermaid. Mermaid is the name of the diagram language; keep it and the middle dot.

diagram.flow.before.description: Label at the start of the first row of a "Before → after" diagram: the steps as they are before the change.

diagram.flow.after.description: Label at the start of the second row of a "Before → after" diagram: the steps as they are once the change is in.

diagram.changes.added.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change adds the thing named on the row.

diagram.changes.changed.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change alters the thing named on the row.

diagram.changes.removed.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change removes the thing named on the row.

diagram.text.rename.description: A rename diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{from}} is the old name and {{to}} the new one, as the change's author wrote them.

diagram.text.renameIn.description: A rename diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{from}} is the old name and {{to}} the new one; {{places}} lists where the name appears (for example "Project name" or the screens the author named), already joined into a list.

diagram.text.flow.description: A "Before → after" diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{before}} and {{after}} are each the steps in order, for example "Vote, then Checks, then Closes".

diagram.text.then.description: How the steps of a "Before → after" diagram follow one another when it is said in words for a screen reader. {{first}} is every step so far and {{second}} the next one; each step is the change author's own words.

diagram.text.added.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change adds {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.addedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change adds {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is the author's short note about it.

diagram.text.changed.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change alters {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.changedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change alters {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is a short note about it.

diagram.text.removed.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change removes {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.removedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change removes {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is a short note about it.

diagram.text.numbers.description: One row of a "Numbers" diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{label}} is what is measured, as the change's author named it; {{before}} and {{after}} are the figures before and after the change, each with its unit (for example "2.4 s").

diagram.text.sentences.description: How the sentences of a diagram said in words follow one another, for a screen reader (one sentence per row of the diagram). {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next whole sentence. Change only what stands between them.

diagram.text.mermaid.text: A diagram drawn from its author’s text.
diagram.text.mermaid.description: What a screen reader hears for a free-form diagram that the change's author wrote in a diagram language (Mermaid) and that cannot be said in words.

diagram.decision.projectName.description: Where the name changes, shown as a small chip under a group decision's rename diagram (old name → new name) on a Needs-you card: the project's name.

diagram.decision.secretRemoved.description: Note beside the setting's name in a group decision's "What changes" diagram on a Needs-you card, when the decision removes a secret setting (an API key or password the project keeps hidden).

diagram.decision.secretChanged.text: A secret setting, value not shown
diagram.decision.secretChanged.description: Note beside the setting's name in a group decision's "What changes" diagram on a Needs-you card, when the decision sets a secret setting (an API key or password the project keeps hidden); its new value is never shown.

places.list.hub.description: First entry in a project's list of places (beside the page on a wide window, in the tray on a phone): the project's overview, with who is here, what is new and what waits on you. A noun, the name of the place.

places.list.needsYou.description: Second entry in a project's list of places: the feed of decisions waiting on this person (changes to vote on, requests nobody has taken). A count may follow it.

places.list.workshop.description: Third entry in a project's list of places: the build page, listing the work going on, the requests and the changes. A noun, the name of the place.

places.list.channels.description: Small upper-case heading in a project's list of places, over the project's own chat channel (#general).

places.list.topics.description: Small upper-case heading in a project's list of places, over its topics: the categories its members set up, each a chat channel of its own.

places.list.switchCommunity.description: Last entry of a project's list of places in the tray on a phone: opens the list of the person's communities to go to another one.

places.list.name.description: Accessible name of a project's list of places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

places.list.nameUnnamed.description: Accessible name of a project's list of places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels) when the project's name is not known yet.

places.list.filtered.description: Read only by screen readers, right after Workshop in a project's list of places, while a search or filter is narrowing the project's All items page. Keep the parentheses.

places.list.countAloud.description: Read only by screen readers after an entry in a project's list of places that shows a number: says what the number counts. {{phrase}} is that, already worded, for example "29 to vote" or "3 unread". Keep the parentheses.

places.list.app.description: First row of a project's places list (the tray behind the place bar, the phone's drawer): opens the project's app, the thing its members build and use. Shown under the project's name, so it says only App.

places.list.appOf.description: Accessible name of that App row, which opens the project's app. {{project}} is the project's name.

places.list.showMore_one.description: Last row under Topics in a project's places, nested under the community in the desktop sidebar (a window 1024px or wider), when the sidebar shows only the first topics: shows the rest. {{count}} is how many more topics there are (here 1).

places.list.showMore_other.description: Last row under Topics in a project's places, nested under the community in the desktop sidebar (a window 1024px or wider), when the sidebar shows only the first topics: shows the rest. {{count}} is how many more topics there are.

places.count.toVote_one.description: What the number beside Needs you in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: changes waiting for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

places.count.toVote_other.description: What the number beside Needs you in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: changes waiting for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

places.count.unread_one.description: The count beside a channel in a project's list of places, shown in its pill, its hover text and to screen readers: messages there this person has not read. {{shown}} is that number as displayed (capped as 99+ on screen); the plural form follows the real count.

places.count.unread_other.description: The count beside a channel in a project's list of places, shown in its pill, its hover text and to screen readers: messages there this person has not read. {{shown}} is that number as displayed (capped as 99+ on screen); the plural form follows the real count.

places.bar.hub.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Hub (or the plan under it) is on show: names the place you are on. A noun, the name of the place.

places.bar.needsYou.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Needs you place is on show: the feed of decisions waiting on this person.

places.bar.workshop.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Workshop (or the All items page under it) is on show: names the place you are on. A noun, the name of the place.

places.bar.button.description: Accessible name of the button on the bar at the top of a project's page that opens the list of the project's places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

places.bar.buttonUnnamed.description: Accessible name of the button on the bar at the top of a project's page that opens the list of the project's places, when the project's name is not known yet.

places.bar.waitingAloud.description: Read only by screen readers after the name of the places button at the top of a project's page, while something in the project waits for this person (a dot is shown). {{waiting}} is what waits, already worded, for example "29 to vote, 4 unread". Keep the parentheses.

places.bar.toVote_one.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: changes waiting for their vote. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.toVote_other.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: changes waiting for their vote. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.unread_one.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: messages in the project's channels they have not read. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.unread_other.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: messages in the project's channels they have not read. {{count}} is how many.

places.mergedCard.text.description: Card in a topic's chat history at the point where another topic was merged into it. {{channel}} is the merged topic's handle, written after its #, for example signup. Keep the # before it.

places.mergedCard.read.description: Link on the card in a topic's chat history that marks where another topic was merged into it: opens the merged topic's old channel, which can still be read. {{channel}} is that topic's handle, written after its #. Keep the # and the arrow.

places.topicHead.mergedInto.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one: its channel can be read but not written in. {{channel}} is the handle of the topic it joined, written after its #. Keep the #.

places.topicHead.mergedIntoLink.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one: its channel can be read but not written in. {{channel}} is the handle of the topic it joined, written after its #; <0></0> makes it a link that opens that topic. Keep the #.

places.topicHead.mergedUnnamed.text: Merged into another topic. Read only.
places.topicHead.mergedUnnamed.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one that cannot be named: its channel can be read but not written in.

places.topicHead.archived.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was archived: its channel can be read but not written in.

places.topicHead.requests_one.description: Link at the top of a topic's chat channel: opens the project's All items page narrowed to the open requests filed under this topic. {{count}} is how many there are. Keep the arrow.

places.topicHead.requests_other.description: Link at the top of a topic's chat channel: opens the project's All items page narrowed to the open requests filed under this topic. {{count}} is how many there are. Keep the arrow.

places.topicHead.aboutThenRequests.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel. {{about}} is what the topic is for, as its members wrote it; <0></0> is a link to the requests filed under it, and {{requests}} its words, already worded, for example "14 requests ›".

places.generalHead.about.description: Line at the top of a project's #general chat channel, saying what the channel is for. {{project}} is the project's name.

places.generalHead.aboutThenMembers.description: Line at the top of a project's #general chat channel: what the channel is for, then how many members it reaches. {{about}} is the first part, already worded ("Where everyone in Homeroom talks"); {{members}} the second, already worded ("263 members").

places.generalHead.members_one.description: Part of the line at the top of a project's #general chat channel: how many people are members of the project, so how many the channel reaches.

places.generalHead.members_other.description: Part of the line at the top of a project's #general chat channel: how many people are members of the project, so how many the channel reaches.

places.generalHead.mute.description: Button at the top of a project's #general chat channel: mutes the channel for you, so its unread messages stop counting and it stops notifying you about every message. Mentions and replies still reach you.

places.generalHead.muted.description: The same button at the top of a project's #general chat channel once you have muted it; pressing it again unmutes the channel.

places.generalHead.muteHint.text: Stop counting unread messages here and stop notifications for every message. Mentions and replies still reach you.
places.generalHead.muteHint.description: Hover text of the Mute button at the top of a project's #general chat channel: says what muting does.

places.generalHead.unmuteHint.text: Muted: unread messages here are not counted. Press to unmute.
places.generalHead.unmuteHint.description: Hover text of the button at the top of a project's #general chat channel while the channel is muted for you.

places.topicFigures.label.description: Accessible name of the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel, such as how long checks take or how often the bot's answers fail.

places.topicFigures.window_one.description: Small heading over the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel: says the numbers cover the last day. Shown in capitals.

places.topicFigures.window_other.description: Small heading over the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel: says how many days the numbers cover, for example "Last 7 days". {{count}} is that number. Shown in capitals.

places.topicFigures.whatItMeans.description: Accessible name of the small information button beside one number's name at the top of a topic's chat channel: shows a sentence explaining that number. {{label}} is the number's name, for example "Reply time".

places.topicFigures.demo.text: Staging demo figures, not real numbers.
places.topicFigures.demo.description: Small line under the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel, shown only on a test copy of Homeroom: says the numbers are made up for testing.

places.topicFigures.folded_one.text: {{figures}}. The other measure appears once {{min}} people are counted.
places.topicFigures.folded_one.description: Quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel in place of the card of numbers, while most numbers still need more people. {{figures}} is the list of the numbers that do have data, for example "Errors in a first session 0% (0 of 18 visits)". {{min}} is how many people a number needs.

places.topicFigures.folded_other.text: {{figures}}. The other {{count}} measures appear once {{min}} people are counted.
places.topicFigures.folded_other.description: Quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel in place of the card of numbers, while most numbers still need more people. {{figures}} is the list of the numbers that do have data, for example "Errors in a first session 0%". {{count}} is how many numbers are still waiting. {{min}} is how many people a number needs.

places.topicFigures.foldedNone_one.text: This measure appears once {{min}} people are counted.
places.topicFigures.foldedNone_one.description: Quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel in place of the card of numbers, while no number has data yet and there is one number. {{min}} is how many people a number needs.

places.topicFigures.foldedNone_other.text: These {{count}} measures appear once {{min}} people are counted.
places.topicFigures.foldedNone_other.description: Quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel in place of the card of numbers, while no number has data yet. {{count}} is how many numbers there are. {{min}} is how many people a number needs.

places.topicFigures.foldedItem.description: One number in the quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel, while most numbers still need more people. {{label}} is the number's name, {{reading}} its value and {{sub}} its detail, for example "Errors in a first session 0% (0 of 18 visits · target under 1%)".

places.topicFigures.foldedInfo.description: Accessible name of the small information button at the end of the quiet line at the top of a topic's chat channel: explains how the numbers are rounded and what "not enough data" means.

places.topicSignals.label.description: Small heading over the list, at the top of a topic's chat channel, of problems Homeroom found in itself and filed as requests, such as a release that stalled. Also the list's accessible name. Shown in capitals.

places.topicSignals.since.description: Part of the grey line under one problem in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel: when Homeroom first noticed the problem. {{when}} is already worded, for example "3h ago", "just now" or "Jun 16". Starts lower case because it follows who is handling the problem and a middle dot.

places.topicSignals.clearing.description: Part of the grey line under one problem in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel, in place of when it was first seen: the problem has stopped happening, and Homeroom is waiting a while to be sure before closing it.

places.topicSignals.times_one.description: Part of the grey line under one problem in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel: how many times Homeroom has seen the problem happen. English shows it only from 2. A translation may use {{count}}, the number of times.

places.topicSignals.times_other.description: Part of the grey line under one problem in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel: how many times Homeroom has seen the problem happen, for example "4 times". {{count}} is that number.

places.topicSignals.details.description: Small link at the end of one problem's row in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel, shown only to Homeroom's admins: opens the part of the admin console that shows more about the problem.

places.topicSignals.detailsLabel.text: Details of {{title}} in the admin console
places.topicSignals.detailsLabel.description: Accessible name of the Details link on one problem's row in the Open problems list of a topic's chat channel, shown only to Homeroom's admins. {{title}} is the problem's one-line description, for example "Release stalled: the deploy workflow failed".

topic.request.shots.hideComment.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the comment pinned to the picture is drawn over it: hides the comment.

topic.request.shots.hideComments.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the several comments pinned to the picture are drawn over it: hides them.

topic.request.shots.showComment.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the comment pinned to the picture is hidden: draws it over the picture again.

topic.request.shots.showComments.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the several comments pinned to the picture are hidden: draws them over the picture again.

touches.kicker.description: Small label at the top of the picture a change's card shows when it has no before and after shots: which parts of the project the change touches, drawn from its files.

touches.files.none.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture, when the change touches no file in it.

touches.files.count_one.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture: how many of the change's files are in it.

touches.files.count_other.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture: how many of the change's files are in it.

touches.area.screens.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: the screens people see (its interface code).

touches.area.server.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its server code.

touches.area.database.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its database schema and data.

touches.area.tests.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its automated tests.

touches.area.docs.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its documentation.

touches.area.other.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: files that belong to none of the other areas.

touches.area.withFiles.description: One area in the spoken description of the "What it touches" picture. {{area}} is the area's name (Screens, Server…) and {{files}} how many files, for example "Server, 2 files".

touches.areas.pair.description: How the areas are joined in the spoken description of the "What it touches" picture, for example "Server, 2 files; Tests, 1 file". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next area. Only the punctuation is translated.

touches.label.description: What a screen reader says for the "What it touches" picture on a change's card: the parts of the project the change touches. {{areas}} lists them, for example "Server, 2 files; Tests, 1 file".

touches.labelNothingVisible.description: The spoken description of the "What it touches" picture when the change's author declared that nothing on screen changes. {{said}} is the description that comes first ("What it touches. Server, 2 files.").

touches.footNothingVisible.text: Nothing on screen changes · drawn from the change’s files
touches.footNothingVisible.description: Line under the "What it touches" picture when the change's author declared that nothing on screen changes; it also says the picture was drawn from the change's files.

menu.topics.title.description: Row in a project's + menu that opens its topics: its lasting conversations, each a channel and a category requests are filed under.

menu.topics.sub.text: The project's channels, and the categories requests are filed under
menu.topics.sub.description: Second line of the Topics row in a project's + menu, saying what topics are.

discussion.topic.none.description: Shown on a project's page when a link names a topic channel the project does not have. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.mergedInto.text: #{{handle}} was merged into #{{into}}. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.mergedInto.description: Notice under a topic channel that was merged into another, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is this channel's short name and {{into}} the one it joined, each shown after #.

discussion.topic.mergedIntoAnother.text: #{{handle}} was merged into another topic. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.mergedIntoAnother.description: Notice under a topic channel that was merged into another one that can no longer be found, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is this channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.archived.text: #{{handle}} is archived. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.archived.description: Notice under an archived topic channel, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.joinToPost.text: Join this community to post here.
discussion.topic.joinToPost.description: Notice under a topic channel for someone who has not joined the project's community, in place of the message box.

discussion.topic.placeholder.description: Placeholder in the message box of a project's topic channel. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.

communityCard.line.youOrGroup.you.some_o.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and you say yes, or {{count}} of the {{total}} active members does.
communityCard.line.youOrGroup.you.some_o.description: Workshop Overview rule line for the project's creator under You or the group: their yes, or the group's vote, here {{count}} of the {{total}} active members, one of them. The wide card's wording.

communityCard.line.twoYeses.description: Workshop Overview rule line under Two yeses. The wide card's wording.

communityCard.lineShort.twoYeses.text: Goes live when its checks pass and two people say yes.
communityCard.lineShort.twoYeses.description: Workshop Overview rule line under Two yeses. The narrow card's wording.

communityCard.lineShort.openFloor.text: Goes live when its checks pass and any member says yes.

menu.whoDecides.title.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the sheet that sets who can see the project and how its changes are approved.

menu.whoDecides.sub.text: Private or public, and how changes are approved
menu.whoDecides.sub.description: Second line of the 'Who can see & change it' row.

topic.thread.ballot.label.description: Spoken name of the one vote between competing changes on a request's or a change's page: two or more changes for the same piece of work (or a change and a proposal to close it) are up for a vote, and the person picks one.

topic.thread.ballot.about.text: The first to pass {{project}}’s approval rule goes live, and the others close. Neither counts as a No on each.
topic.thread.ballot.about.description: Line under the one vote between competing changes: how it is decided. {{project}} is the project's name.

topic.thread.ballot.neither.description: The last choice of the ballot between competing changes: the person wants none of them to go live (it votes No on each).

topic.thread.page.someone.description: Stands in for a person's name on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close, when the name is not known.

topic.thread.page.change.description: Small-caps line over one change on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close that has no number yet. {{by}} is who built it (a username, or Homeroom bot).

topic.thread.page.changeNumbered.description: Small-caps line over one change on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close. {{number}} is the change's number, {{by}} who built it (a username, or Homeroom bot). The change's title follows on the next line.

topic.thread.page.changeLettered.description: Small-caps line over one of several competing changes on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close. {{letter}} is the change's letter (A, B, C), {{by}} who built it.

topic.thread.page.changeLoading.description: Read by a screen reader while a request's page loads the section about the change built for it: its status pill, its title and its Votes and Testing cards, drawn as a grey outline until they arrive.

topic.thread.page.underway.text: Being built. Its votes open once it is up for a vote.
topic.thread.page.underway.description: Line under a change on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close that is still being built, where its Votes and Testing cards will be.

topic.thread.page.ready.text: Built, and its checks pass. Its votes open once it is put up for a vote.
topic.thread.page.ready.description: Line under a change on a request's page, where its Votes and Testing cards will be: the change has finished building and its checks pass, and nothing happens until it is put up for a vote.

topic.thread.page.rowBy.description: Second line of one competing change's row on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close: who built it and the change's number.

topic.thread.page.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button on the line of a change that has no number yet, on its request's page (where a change built for a request is shown, in place of a page of its own): opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the change, such as Details or Edit description.

topic.thread.page.moreNumbered.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button on a change's line, on its request's page (where a change built for a request is shown, in place of a page of its own): opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the change, such as Details or Edit description. {{number}} is the change's number.

topic.thread.page.shotBefore.description: Label on the small picture of how the project looked before a change, beside the one of how it looks after, on the change's section of its request's page. Tapping either opens the before and after viewer.

topic.thread.page.shotAfter.description: Label on the small picture of how the project looks with a change, beside the one of how it looked before, on the change's section of its request's page. Tapping either opens the before and after viewer.

topic.thread.page.shotsOpen.description: Accessible name of the pair of small before and after pictures on a change's section of its request's page: opens the before and after viewer over the page.

topic.thread.page.shotsExpand.description: Button beside the small before and after pictures on a change's section of its request's page: opens the before and after viewer over the page, at nearly the window's size. The same word the viewer's own Expand button uses.

topic.thread.page.claims.description: Small line over the card on a request's page for a change that lives on another request's page and lists this request among the ones it closes. {{number}} is the change's number; <0></0> links to the change where it lives.

topic.thread.page.claimsUnnumbered.description: Small line over the card on a request's page for a change that has no number yet, lives on another request's page, and lists this request among the ones it closes. <0></0> links to the change where it lives.

topic.thread.page.claimDispute.description: Button on the card for a change that says it closes the viewer's request. Only the request's requester sees it. Pressing it records their disagreement and posts a line in the change's discussion; it does not unlink the request.

topic.thread.page.claimDisputed.text: You said this doesn't close it
topic.thread.page.claimDisputed.description: Line in place of the "This doesn't close it" button on the card for a change that says it closes the viewer's request, after the requester pressed it. Shown only to the requester.

topic.thread.page.claimNotConfirmed.description: After another request's number under a change that closes it, when that request's requester answered "This doesn't close it": the change still lists it, but the requester says the change does not close it.

topic.thread.page.claimDisputeFailed.description: Error line under the "This doesn't close it" button when recording the requester's answer failed.

topic.thread.page.alsoCloses.description: Under a change's title on a request's page: the other requests it will close when it merges. <0></0> is the list of request numbers, each a link to its page, possibly ending in "N more".

topic.thread.page.alsoClosed.description: Under a change's title on a request's page, once the change has merged: the other requests it closed. <0></0> is the list of request numbers, each a link to its page, possibly ending in "N more".

topic.thread.page.alsoMore_one.description: Last item of the list of other requests a change also closes, on its request's page, when one request is hidden. Tapping it shows the hidden numbers in the same line.

topic.thread.page.alsoMore_other.description: Last item of the list of other requests a change also closes, on its request's page, when some are hidden. Tapping it shows the hidden numbers in the same line.

topic.thread.page.closesOf_one.text: Closes {{count}} of the {{total}} requests in this thread
topic.thread.page.closesOf_one.description: Under a change's title on a request's page, when the thread holds several requests and the change closes only some of them: {{count}} is how many it closes, {{total}} how many the thread holds.

topic.thread.page.closesOf_other.text: Closes {{count}} of the {{total}} requests in this thread
topic.thread.page.closesOf_other.description: Under a change's title on a request's page, when the thread holds several requests and the change closes only some of them: {{count}} is how many it closes, {{total}} how many the thread holds.

topic.thread.page.partOf_one.description: Under a request's title on its page, when its thread holds several requests: it is one of them. {{count}} is how many requests the thread holds, {{name}} the thread's name, a link to the request whose page the thread opens on.

topic.thread.page.partOf_other.description: Under a request's title on its page, when its thread holds several requests: it is one of them. {{count}} is how many requests the thread holds, {{name}} the thread's name, a link to the request whose page the thread opens on.

topic.thread.ballot.close.description: A choice of the one vote between a request's changes and a proposal to close the request, in place of Neither: the person wants the request closed with none of the changes.

topic.thread.ballot.heading.description: Small-caps heading over competing changes on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close. {{n}} is how many changes (two or more), {{number}} the request's number.

topic.thread.ballot.headingClose.description: Small-caps heading on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close when one change and a proposal to close the request compete in one vote.

topic.thread.ballot.headingCloseMany.description: Small-caps heading on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close when several changes and a proposal to close the request compete in one vote. {{n}} is how many changes.

topic.thread.ballot.votes.description: Name of the card that holds a vote on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close, as a change's own Votes card is named.

topic.thread.ballot.yourPick.description: Figure in the corner of the one vote between competing changes, before the person has picked one.

topic.thread.ballot.picked.description: Figure in the corner of the one vote between competing changes, once the person has picked one (they can still change it).

topic.thread.ballot.tally.description: Spoken name of one bar of the vote between competing changes. {{choice}} is the choice (A, B, Close it), {{yes}} its yes votes, {{need}} what the project's approval rule needs.

topic.thread.ballot.aboutClose.text: The first to pass {{project}}’s approval rule wins: the change goes live, or the request closes.
topic.thread.ballot.aboutClose.description: Line under the one vote between a request's changes and a proposal to close it: how it is decided. {{project}} is the project's name.

topic.thread.close.kicker.description: Small-caps line over a proposal to close the request on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close. {{by}} is who proposed it. Its reason follows.

topic.thread.close.by.description: Second line of the Close it row of the vote between a request's changes and closing it. {{by}} is who proposed closing it.

topic.thread.close.byWhy.description: Second line of the Close it row of the vote between a request's changes and closing it. {{by}} is who proposed it, {{reason}} their reason in their own words.

topic.thread.close.votes.description: Spoken name of the Votes card of a proposal to close the request, on a request's page, under the request: its changes and its vote to close.

topic.thread.close.figure.description: Figure in the corner of the Votes card of a proposal to close the request: {{yes}} yes votes so far of the {{need}} the project's approval rule needs.

topic.thread.close.yes.description: Button on the Votes card of a proposal to close the request: vote yes, close it.

topic.thread.close.no.description: Button on the Votes card of a proposal to close the request: vote no, keep it open.

topic.thread.close.note.text: If it passes, every request here closes, and the changes up for a vote close with them.
topic.thread.close.note.description: Line under the Votes card of a proposal to close the request, before the person has voted: what happens if the vote passes.

topic.thread.close.saidYes.text: You said yes. If it passes, every request here closes.
topic.thread.close.saidYes.description: Line under the Votes card of a proposal to close the request, once the person voted yes.

topic.thread.close.saidNo.description: Line under the Votes card of a proposal to close the request, once the person voted no.

topic.thread.close.closedByVote.description: First words of the line under a request's vote to close it, once the vote has ended: the group voted to close the request, and it closed.

topic.thread.close.keptOpen.description: First words of the line under a request's vote to close it, once the vote has ended: the vote was withdrawn or could not be applied, so the request stays open.

topic.thread.close.closedElsewhere.text: Ended: the request closed another way.
topic.thread.close.closedElsewhere.description: First words of the line under a request's vote to close it, once the vote has ended because the request closed another way (a change merged, or it was closed on GitHub).

topic.thread.close.showAll.description: Button under a request's vote to close it, under the first few replies people posted on the vote: opens the rest of them.

topic.thread.pill.choosing.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: two or more changes (or a change and a proposal to close it) are up for one vote between them.

topic.thread.pill.vote.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a change built for it is up for a vote.

topic.thread.pill.close.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a proposal to close the request is up for a vote.

topic.thread.pill.ready.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a change for it has finished building and its checks pass, and it waits to be put up for a vote.

topic.thread.pill.building.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a change for it is being built.

topic.thread.pill.readyToBuild.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: Homeroom bot is ready to build the change for it and the build waits its turn, so nothing is being built yet.

topic.thread.pill.live.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a change built for it went live.

topic.thread.pill.goingLive.description: Status pill beside a request's number in its page's header: a change built for it merged and is on its way to production, not running yet.

topic.thread.page.changeNumberedPr.description: Small-caps line over one change on a request's page, under the request, on a project whose code is on GitHub (where a change's number is GitHub's pull request number, written PR, never #): its changes and its vote to close. {{number}} is the change's number, {{by}} who built it (a username, or Homeroom bot). The change's title follows on the next line.

topic.thread.page.moreNumberedPr.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button on a change's line on its request's page, on a project whose code is on GitHub (a change's number is written PR, never #): opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the change, such as Details or Edit description. {{number}} is the change's number.

topic.thread.page.rowByPr.description: Second line of one competing change's row on a request's page, on a project whose code is on GitHub (a change's number is written PR, never #): who built it and the change's number.

topic.thread.page.claimsPr.description: Small line over the card on a request's page for a change that lives on another request's page and lists this request among the ones it closes, on a project whose code is on GitHub (a change's number is written PR, never #). {{number}} is the change's number; <0></0> links to the change where it lives.

topic.request.stream.onChangePr.description: Small words after the time of a reply or a line in a request's discussion that was written on one of the request's changes, on a project whose code is on GitHub (a change's number is written PR, never #): the request's page holds the discussion of the whole piece of work. {{number}} is the change's number.

topic.decision.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the sheet on a governance vote's page, announced by screen readers: the page for one decision the project votes on.

topic.decision.bar.rename.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to rename the project. {{number}} is the vote's number.

topic.decision.bar.secret.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to change one of the project's secrets. {{number}} is the vote's number.

topic.decision.bar.campaign.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to run a maintenance campaign on the project. {{number}} is the vote's number.

topic.decision.bar.illustration.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to change the picture on the project's card. {{number}} is the vote's number.

topic.decision.bar.close.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to close a request. {{number}} is the vote's number. A request is what people file asking for work; never say issue.

topic.decision.bar.reopen.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to bring back a closed request. {{number}} is the vote's number. A request is what people file asking for work; never say issue.

topic.decision.bar.move.description: Small line above the title in the header of a governance vote's page, for a vote to merge or split discussions. {{number}} is the vote's number.

topic.decision.bar.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the header of a governance vote's page: opens the menu with Copy link and, for the person who proposed it, Withdraw.

topic.decision.rename.fromTo.description: What a vote to rename the project does, as a sentence under the vote's title. {{from}} is the project's current name and {{to}} the proposed one; <0></0> and <1></1> make each name bold.

topic.decision.secret.set.text: Sets the secret <0>{{key}}</0>. Its value is never shown.
topic.decision.secret.set.description: What a vote to change one of the project's secrets does, under the vote's title. {{key}} is the secret's name, in capitals; <0></0> sets it in code style. The value is deliberately not shown to anyone.

topic.decision.secret.remove.text: Removes the secret <0>{{key}}</0>. Its value is never shown.
topic.decision.secret.remove.description: What a vote to remove one of the project's secrets does, under the vote's title. {{key}} is the secret's name, in capitals; <0></0> sets it in code style.

topic.decision.campaign.empty.description: Line under a maintenance campaign vote's title when the campaign was filed without an explanation of what it does.

topic.decision.close.request.description: Line under a vote to close a request, naming the request it would close. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title; <0></0> sets the number in bold. A request is what people file asking for work; never say issue.

topic.decision.votes.label.description: Accessible name of the card on a governance vote's page that shows the tally and offers Yes and No.

topic.decision.votes.name.description: Heading of the card on a governance vote's page that shows the tally and offers Yes and No.

topic.decision.votes.figure.description: The count beside the heading of the Votes card on a governance vote's page: how many people said yes and how many the rule needs.

topic.decision.votes.note.text: Needs {{need}} yes votes. It applies when the vote passes.
topic.decision.votes.note.description: Line under the Votes card on an open governance vote's page, saying how many yes votes the rule needs and what happens then.

topic.decision.outcome.applied.text: Passed and applied. Voting has ended.
topic.decision.outcome.applied.description: Line under the Votes card on a governance vote's page once the vote passed and the change was carried out.

topic.decision.outcome.applying.text: Passed. It is being applied now.
topic.decision.outcome.applying.description: Line under the Votes card on a governance vote's page once the vote passed and the change is being carried out at this moment.

topic.decision.outcome.refused.description: Line under the Votes card on a governance vote's page once the vote ended without passing, or the change was refused.

topic.decision.outcome.withdrawn.description: Line under the Votes card on a governance vote's page once the person who proposed it took it back.

topic.decision.outcome.superseded.text: No longer needed. Voting has ended.
topic.decision.outcome.superseded.description: Line under the Votes card on a governance vote's page once something else settled what it was about, so the vote no longer applies.
